ABOUT CAPE

Cape is America’s privacy-first mobile carrier. Our mission is to be a force for good in global wireless. Cape was founded in 2022 by people who believe privacy is a fundamental right, not a luxury to be traded away. Our journey began when our founder recognized a critical vulnerability in our modern world: everyone relies on the same stagnant cellular infrastructure and legacy systems that track our every movement, monitor and profile our connections, and lose and sell our personal data.

Instead of accepting the status quo, we decided to fix it. National security professionals, journalists, parents, and everyone in between can stay connected and have privacy.

We didn’t just build a layer on top of old tech; we built America’s most private and secure mobile carrier from the ground up. By building our own network from scratch, we are able to design and build a suite of privacy and security features that no other carrier on the planet can offer.

Today, Cape provides our secure network to consumers, businesses, and government agencies alike. We closed our Series C in March 2026, and we are scaling rapidly, with the goal of giving people back control of their most personal information.




THE TEAM

At Cape, we are the architects of a privacy-centric movement that is just getting started. We are relentless builders, constantly innovating at the edge of what's possible in telecommunications. We operate on a foundation of high trust and high expectations. Our structure is flat, and collaboration matters more than hierarchy. As a member of our team, you will collaborate with world-class engineers, architects, and visionaries, and work across organizational lines to solve "impossible" problems and deliver mission-critical results for our users every single day.




THE ROLE

You write Cape into public narratives. Policymakers, government and enterprise decisionmakers, and thought leaders in defense and security will recognize Cape as innovators with current, fresh, and influential ideas and contributions to a nation grappling with connected and autonomous warfare, surveillance, and AI-empowered threats to critical infrastructure. You will weave together threads from your sales and engineering colleagues, bringing technical accomplishments and wins in key strategic accounts into the story of how modern wars will be fought on cellular infrastructure, with Cape as the central actor helping America gain and secure the edge.

You’ll also grow Cape’s brand with consumers, working with product and marketing colleagues to explain Cape’s features and, more importantly, to convey our values.

You would manage our PR outreach across both Tier 1 and trade outlets, write and research original content from blog posts to op-eds to whitepapers across earned media and owned channels, develop relationships with external third-parties who can help validate our story, and manage Cape’s participation in key events.

 - Progressive Network Engineering Experience: 8+ years of progressive network engineering experience, including experience leading design efforts on cross-team initiatives.

 - Large-Scale Data Center Expertise: Experience designing or operating networks at 1000+ switches across multi-site environments.

 - Routing Knowledge: Strong routing knowledge, including solid proficiency in BGP, EVPN/VXLAN, OSPF, ECMP, BFD, and modern data center routing design.

 - SDN & Programmability: Hands-on experience with an SDN controller and network programmability via NETCONF/YANG, RESTCONF, or gNMI.

About the Role:

You will partner with the Physical Network Automation team to design the automation frameworks, self-healing workflows, and observability platforms that allow our global fleet to scale sublinearly with headcount.



This is a senior technical leadership role at the intersection of Architecture, Software Engineering, and Infrastructure Reliability. You will work side by side with the Physical Network Automation team, combining Architecture's design perspective with their operational and implementation expertise, to turn intent-based designs into production automation. You will also represent Architecture in cross-functional planning with Deployment, Operations, and Site Reliability. You're not writing scripts to replace manual tasks. You're helping design the control plane model that makes our infrastructure intelligent.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Co-Develop the Automation Architecture: Partner with the Physical Network Automation team to shape the technical roadmap and reference architecture for Crusoe's automation stack, from source of truth and configuration generation through day-2 operations, telemetry, and closed-loop remediation.

 - Shape the Source of Truth: Work with automation and operations teams on the data model that drives configuration, validation, and operational state, and help establish how systems integrate with it.

 - Design Intent-Based Systems Together: Collaborate on declarative, model-driven configuration pipelines that treat infrastructure as code and make configuration drift impossible, contributing architectural direction while the automation team brings implementation and operational insight.

 - Contribute to Model-Driven Standards: Help define the approach to API-driven, schema-defined telemetry collection, configuration management, and state validation across heterogeneous hardware and vendors.

 - Design Self-Healing Workflows: Work jointly on the architecture for event-driven, auto-remediation systems that detect faults, correlate telemetry, and resolve known failure modes without human escalation.

 - Shape the Observability Strategy: Partner on the technical direction for telemetry, metrics, alerting, and dashboarding, including streaming pipelines and the data models behind them.

 - Advocate for Automation-First Design: Work with network architects and automation engineers so that designs are deployable, validatable, and operable programmatically at scale from day one.

 - Collaborate and Multiply: Participate in design reviews, architecture reviews, and technical discussions that raise the engineering bar across both teams, learning from the automation team as much as guiding them.



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 12+ years of engineering experience with a demonstrated focus on production software engineering, platform architecture, and infrastructure as code in hyperscale or internet-scale environments.

 - Demonstrated Technical Leadership: Proven track record of helping define architectures for automation platforms that a broader engineering organization builds on, and of influencing and aligning teams you don't directly manage.

 - Strong Software Engineering Foundation: Fluency in Python or Go, with a clear understanding of what makes systems testable, CI/CD-integrated, and production-ready. You can review and contribute to implementation, and prototype when needed.

 - Model-Driven Automation Fluency: Deep experience with declarative, schema-defined configuration and telemetry, and a clear view of why model-driven automation is the only path to hyperscale.

We are rebuilding the financial infrastructure that real economy operators rely on. We’re a Series B startup backed by Lachy Groom, Thrive Capital, Dylan Field, Thomson Reuters Ventures, Cameron Ventures, and leaders at Notion, Gusto, and Vercel. We’re looking for team members to help us untangle the intersection of American industry, climate, and the economy.




THE OPPORTUNITY

We're hiring our founding RevOps Lead, reporting to Chris Brouwer https://www.linkedin.com/in/cebrouwer/, our Head of Revenue, to design and run the operating system for Ambrook's commercial business. You'll own HubSpot and every commercial tool around it, across marketing, sales, partnerships and success, as one team. The job is to make our data, systems and operating rhythm good enough that people and agents can answer "do we have enough MQLs and reps to hit the number?" or "which experiments do we double down on, and which do we drop?" in minutes.

Our funnel doesn't look like most B2B software. Our customers are farmers, ranchers and rural operators. Scaled paid media, word of mouth, referrals and search feed a self-serve motion with sales assist, and fintech (Wallet, payments, cards) and services (Full Service bookkeeping, Ambrook Tax) revenue sit on top of the software. That makes conversion plumbing, attribution and product-usage signals core to this seat, and the systems you design now also have to carry an outbound motion and a move upmarket next.

This is a player-coach role for a builder. You'll ship commercial integrations and agents yourself, decide when an agent beats deterministic code, and measure what they deliver in hours saved, cycle time, errors and revenue. You'll set the bar for how the whole commercial org uses AI.

You'll also run the mechanics of our commercial operating rhythm: weekly reporting, forecast inputs, commission and planning data, delivered on time with baseline commentary that business leads and Finance take forward. And you'll make metrics like NRR, GRR and CAC payback trustworthy as the team grows.




WITHIN 1 MONTH YOU'LL…

 - Ship your first production automation.

 - Agree how you'll work with our Data team and the platform engineering pod, including the review guardrails for what you build.


WITHIN 3 MONTHS YOU'LL…

 - Publish the HubSpot data model and lifecycle definitions, fix the handoffs between marketing, sales and success, and define our core commercial metrics with one owner each.

 - Launch a v1 weekly forecast and capacity model with Finance, and deliver weekly reporting and forecast inputs on schedule.

 - Take over commission calculation end to end and automate it, and take over deal desk.

 - Put your first agents into production with owners and evals, and write a view on agents vs. code vs. humans for each step of the funnel.

 - Stand up a commercial systems roadmap with intake and a regular release cadence, and agree a shared experiment readout template and attribution rules with Data.


WITHIN 6 MONTHS YOU'LL…

 - Own the commercial systems layer and its integrations across HubSpot, BigQuery, Intercom, Linear and our internal APIs, with core HubSpot data complete and trusted, and every weekly metric tracing to one definition.

 - Run multiple agents in production, reporting their impact in hours, cycle time, errors and revenue, and bring speed-to-lead down to minutes.

 - Make the forecast reliably accurate for a full quarter, including busy season, and break down every miss by driver within a week of close.

 - Automate discount approvals and deal standards so they're auditable, and make sure every commercial experiment launches with a pre-committed metric and a readout.

 - Run a monthly systems review with team leads, and get teams running their own analysis on the system so ad hoc asks trend down.

You can read more about our mission, vision, and programming at astera.org/vision http://astera.org/vision.




PROJECT SUMMARY: 

We are building a frontier robotics lab at Astera Institute. We believe neuroscience and AI will converge in embodied intelligence: animals and robots face shared challenges of perceiving their surroundings, navigating, manipulating objects, and using memory and reasoning to accomplish tasks in the physical world. Robotics provides a powerful testbed for investigating how biological neural circuits solve these challenges and for developing AI systems that turn perception, learning, and cognition into effective action.

Our strategy starts with developing a mechanistic understanding of how neural circuits can generate intelligent behavior, and applying specific mechanism to make robots useful. We aim to continually expand the repertoire of behaviors a robot can perform reliably in real environments, while improving its ability to learn new skills, adapt to changing conditions, and recover from failure. These practical capabilities provide both measurable outcomes and a foundation for investigating deeper principles of intelligence.




POSITION SUMMARY:

We are seeking a Research Scientist to find how specific fly circuits produce behavior and to turn those mechanisms into models that run on robots. We don't simulate the whole brain. We study modular circuits one at a time. Each project starts with neurons that experiments have linked to a behavior. We then use the connectome to find candidate circuit motifs and to rule out mechanisms the wiring can't support, and we test competing models against neural data, in simulation, and then apply them on physical robots. We welcome applicants from neuroscience, engineering, physics, computer science, and related quantitative fields. This position reports to Chongxi Lai, who leads Astera's Robotics team. 

This is a full-time position.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Choose tractable circuits from the literature. Review experimental studies to find behaviors with strong neuron–behavior evidence, such as recordings, activation or silencing experiments, and behavioral assays. Judge which circuits are ready for mechanistic modeling.

 - Use the connectome to generate and constrain hypotheses. Find the identified neurons in the connectome. Trace their inputs, outputs, and recurrent connections, and pull out candidate circuit motifs. Use the wiring to rule out mechanisms the anatomy can't support, and be clear about what it leaves open, such as synapse sign and strength, neuromodulation, and intrinsic dynamics.

 - Build and compare competing circuit models. Test models against neural recordings, behavioral measurements, and perturbation data to find which mechanisms explain the behavior and which circuit elements are necessary.

 - Test models in closed loop, in simulated fruit fly or robots. Work with robotics researchers to put models into simulated and physical bodies. Measure how behavior changes with sensory cues, body dynamics, noise, and task demands.

 - Make predictions for new fly experiments. Use closed-loop results to refine models and derive quantitative predictions. Work with experimental collaborators to design perturbations that distinguish competing models.

 - Help apply learnt mechanisms to robotics. Turn validated circuit mechanisms into algorithms, or algorithmic principles for robot perception, learning, or control on navigation or manipulation tasks.

 - Build a reusable workflow. Develop shared tools and analysis pipelines so each new circuit goes faster than the last. Share models, code, and findings.




QUALIFICATIONS:

Required

 - PhD or equivalent research experience in neuroscience, computer science, physics, applied mathematics, engineering, or a related quantitative field.

 - Demonstrated experience building mechanistic models of neural circuits that are constrained by, and tested against, experimental data.

 - Ability to read experimental literature critically: weigh the strength of neuron–behavior evidence, interpret recordings and perturbations, and turn them into testable predictions that distinguish competing mechanisms.

 - Ability to make principled modeling choices with incomplete data, such as wiring diagram with approximate synaptic counts but without exact synaptic weights and to state which conclusions depend on those choices.

 - Strong programming and quantitative skills, such as dynamical systems, statistical inference, graph analysis, optimization, or machine learning. Experience building reproducible scientific analyses and simulations.

 - Interest in embodied intelligence and ability to collaborate across neuroscience, AI, and robotics.

Bonus Experience

 - Familiarity with Drosophila neuroanatomy, behavior, or genetic tools. Hands-on experience with connectome datasets (e.g., FlyWire, hemibrain, MANC, BANC), including matching experimentally characterized neurons to reconstructed cells.

 - Experience modeling recurrent dynamics, plasticity, neuromodulation, or sensorimotor feedback.

 - Experience with embodied simulation (e.g., NeuroMechFly, flybody, MuJoCo, IsaacSim), physical robots, robot learning, or control, including models that interact with body mechanics.

 - A record of theoretical predictions that were tested experimentally, ideally with experimental collaborators.

THE ROLE

Baseten's GPU fleet will more than double over the next six months, across clusters delivered by neocloud (GPU cloud) providers and clusters we design, procure, and build ourselves (basemetal). Late materials are one of the main reasons clusters slip: GPU systems, RoCE switches and optics, and the CPU, storage, and firewall nodes that make up each cluster's control plane. Every day a cluster is late is contracted capacity we cannot sell.

We're building basemetal +: applying our own technical, supply chain, and delivery expertise to neocloud clusters instead of relying only on the provider's plan. As our first Supply Chain Manager, you will own the materials side of that model. You will own BOMs for basemetal clusters and neocloud control planes from quote to delivery on site, and build the supply chain intelligence our Delivery Managers use to shape proposals, plan schedules, and unblock providers.

This is a build-from-scratch role on the Capacity Supply Operations team. You will define the process, tooling, and supplier relationships, and run them day to day.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own BOMs from quote to delivery: Quote, order, and track materials for basemetal clusters and neocloud control planes, including CPU nodes, VAST storage, firewalls, and RoCE fabric (east-west and north-south switches and optics). Track every line from purchase order to estimated, committed, and actual delivery on site.

 - Run control plane and network readiness: Stand up and operate our model for getting control plane and network materials ahead of GPUs. This includes pre-purchased standard kits held in stock and shipped to a site once GPU delivery dates are set, and predefined BOMs that providers buy through channel partners such as WWT, with lead times built into the schedule.

 - Track lead times: Maintain current lead times for the core components of the NVIDIA reference architecture across compute, network, CPU, and storage, and make them available to Delivery Managers and Engineering.

 - Qualify alternate parts: Identify which OEMs can ship sooner with fewer delivery problems, confirm alternates are accepted under the reference architecture, and switch suppliers mid-delivery when it protects a date (for example, substituting the Arista 7010TX for the NVIDIA MSN2201 management switch).

 - Shape proposals: Feed lead-time and part data into due diligence so Delivery Managers can shape provider proposals around what can actually land on time, including alternate networking and control plane parts.

 - Validate provider orders: Confirm that neocloud providers have ordered all required materials, paid required deposits, and have ship and delivery dates that fit the cluster schedule.

 - Build OEM relationships: Establish and maintain relationships with key suppliers such as NVIDIA, Supermicro, Arista, Cisco, and distributors. Escalate through those relationships to get priority when providers are blocked.

 - Manage logistics: Coordinate freight, receiving, staging, and delivery to site for basemetal builds and stocked kits, and hand off to Asset Management for tagging and tracking.

 - Score suppliers: Build supplier scorecards on lead time accuracy and delivery performance, and feed them to Vendor Management to guide which suppliers providers use.

 - Report risk early: Flag materials risks into the weekly delivery cadence before they become slips, with clear impact on RFS dates and options to recover.

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 7+ years in supply chain, procurement, or materials management for data center, networking, or server hardware.

 - Hands-on experience buying and expediting GPU servers, network switches, optics and transceivers, and storage systems.

 - Experience managing purchase orders and delivery commitments with OEMs, ODMs, and distributors, and holding them to dates.

 - Track record building lead-time tracking and BOM management processes, not only running existing ones.

 - Strong analytical skills. Comfortable owning large BOMs and delivery trackers in spreadsheets or BI tools.

 - Clear, direct communicator who can turn a supply problem into a decision-ready update with options.

 - Comfortable operating with ambiguity in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Working knowledge of NVIDIA reference architectures, including InfiniBand and RoCE v2 (Spectrum-X) fabrics, and the control plane components around them.

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Bedrock Robotics is hiring a Data Scientist to lead the work on Simulation: measuring how realistic our simulator is, and when its results can be trusted. In this role, you will operate as a senior technical individual contributor, partnering closely with simulation, autonomy, machine learning, and evaluation teams to compare simulated runs with real-world data generated by autonomous construction machines and their operators.



You will own the statistical methods behind simulation-based testing (realism metrics, calibration against field data, and the design of simulation experiments) while helping establish foundational practices for how data science is applied at Bedrock. This role is ideal for a senior-to-staff-level data scientist with a strong statistics foundation and experience with simulation or physical systems, who enjoys working close to the engineers building the simulator.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own data science for simulation, focusing on the gaps between simulation and the field that most affect release decisions

 - Analyze field logs and simulated runs side by side to find where simulated machine, soil, and truck behavior departs from reality

 - Define and track realism metrics that compare distributions of simulated and real behavior (cycle times, bucket fill, arm trajectories, soil response, truck interactions) across simulator versions

 - Design simulation experiments (number of runs, scenario mix, variance reduction, sequential tests) so comparisons between software versions are powered and unbiased

 - Collaborate closely with simulation and data engineering teams to extract scenarios from field logs and keep simulated and real data comparable

 - Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, influencing roadmap and design decisions

 - Contribute to the foundation of data science practices at Bedrock, helping shape how future work and teams scale

 - Validate simulation as a predictor: measure how well simulation results predict field outcomes of software releases, and set when a simulation result is strong enough to act on

 - Calibrate simulator parameters (for example terrain material properties) against field data, with uncertainty

 - Find which parts of the simulator (soil physics, hydraulics, sensors, other agents) drive the gap to reality, and help simulation engineers prioritize fixes

 - Build scenario sampling so simulated test suites represent field conditions, and use importance sampling to estimate rare-event rates






WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required

 - Experience validating a simulator or physical model against real-world data

 - 5+ years of experience in data science, applied statistics, or applied machine learning, including work on simulation or physical systems

 - Comfort operating as a senior IC in a fast-growing startup, balancing execution with technical judgment and prioritization

 - Ability to work independently, define analytical approaches, and drive projects from concept to insight

 - Experience working with complex, high-volume time-series data from robots, vehicles, or other physical systems

 - Strong grounding in statistics: experimental design, variance estimation, comparing distributions, and calibrating models to data, with a track record of influencing decisions through data

 - Hands-on experience collaborating with simulation, data engineering, and infrastructure teams on data pipelines, data quality, and scalable analysis workflows

 - Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience using modern tooling like agentic AI

 - Master’s degree in Statistics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field



Preferred

 - Experience with simulation for autonomous vehicles or robotics (realism metrics, simulated agents, scenario-based testing)

 - Experience with physics simulation, multibody dynamics, or granular materials

 - Experience with rare-event estimation, importance sampling, or surrogate models (e.g., Gaussian processes)

 - Experience with learned or generative world models

 - PhD in a quantitative field

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Build end-to-end production workflows that push FLUX to its limits — experiments, visual explorations, and pieces tailored to brand, agency, and entertainment use cases that show what's possible before anyone else figures it out.

 - Background in brand, agency, or film/VFX work — you understand the real process behind shipping professional creative.

 - Working knowledge of Python for scripting and rapid prototyping.

 - Active presence in the creative AI community (X, Discord, YouTube) — you're already someone people follow for generative AI work.

 - Experience creating content that got real traction in the AI/creative space.

 - Experience supporting Sales or GTM teams with creative assets and technical feasibility assessments.

Senior Product Manager, Financial Statement Suite

Before a company publishes its annual report, finance teams have to turn financial data into a complete set of statements and disclosures. Balances need to be mapped, figures carried forward and updated, and supporting information brought together into a draft. Auditors then check that the notes match the primary statements, this year reconciles with last year, and every total adds up. Preparing and reviewing those statements takes days of detailed work, and errors can carry through into a published report.

Today, audit teams rely on Financial Statement Suite (FSS) to read statements, run checks, and show reviewers what it found and where, so they can make the call and stand behind it. The opportunity goes beyond reconciliation: helping auditors and financial professionals review drafts, connect figures to supporting evidence, and manage changes through to sign-off.

You'll own what FSS becomes across preparation and review cycles. You'll decide what sits on the teams roadmap and define strategy for this high opportunity area working with engineering, design, audit experts and the firms who use FSS every day.




ABOUT DATASNIPPER

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust.

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

And we build at scale. More than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on DataSnipper, including Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. In 2025 alone, the DataSnipper platform delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to is customers. Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way.

 




WHAT IMPACT YOU WILL HAVE

 - Own the end-to-end strategy and decisions for our financial statements product, with clear domain ownership

 - Lead product direction in a key area with direct and clear business impact

 - Reimagine how auditors and financial professionals work, making their workflows more defensible
   
   


WHY IT'S AN EXCITING CHALLENGE

 - Reviewers are sceptical, and they should be. A finding they can't trace is a finding they check again by hand.

 - Statements differ by country, by standard and by firm. FSS has to be right on all of them, not just the ones in front of you this week.

 - Firms use FSS when the stakes are highest. Every change has to make their next busy season better, not riskier.

 - Everyone has a request: firms, sales, partners and engineering. You'll decide which ones the evidence supports, and say no to the rest.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The full FS experience: how a team moves through a draft, from the first finding to sign-off

 - Trust in every check: each finding shows what it compared, where the figures came from, and who reviewed it

 - Quality: what "ready to ship" means for each check, and how the team knows a change helps without breaking something else

 - Where FSS goes next: which statement types, standards and markets come first, and why

 - Set the plan and make trade-offs explicit, including new checks versus improving the ones customers already rely on

 - Work with engineering and audit experts on sets of real statements that every change has to pass

About the Role

As part of a lean, highly collaborative IT team, you'll support a fast-scaling global workforce and help drive automation, security, and operational excellence across the business. We're looking for an IT Engineer to be the hands-on IT presence for our London office and the first point of contact for IT across EMEA.

You'll be the only IT team member in London, five hours ahead of our IT teammate in New York and eight hours ahead of San Francisco. You'll resolve tickets and day-to-day issues yourself, and scope and align on larger projects with the team before building. Expect occasional calls outside UK hours.

Automation is the core of the job. You'll co-own identity and access management, endpoint administration, and SaaS operations for the company, using Serval, our AI-native service management platform, to turn recurring requests into workflows that resolve themselves. If a request shows up twice, the second time should be the last time anyone handles it by hand.

In this role, you will

 - Serve as the on-site IT engineer for our London office and the go-to IT contact for employees across EMEA, resolving hardware, account, and access issues in person and through the ticket queue

 - Build, test, and maintain Serval workflows for access requests, onboarding and offboarding, password and MFA resets, and other recurring requests

 - Review the automations Serval suggests from ticket history, and decide what gets published and what approvals each one needs

 - Track which requests still need a human, and use ticket data to choose what to automate next

 - Co-own the employee identity lifecycle through Okta so that onboarding, offboarding, and access changes are accurate and on time, with time-bound access and approval rules that make least privilege the default

 - Configure and maintain SSO, SAML, OIDC, and SCIM integrations as we bring on new SaaS applications

 - Administer and evolve our core SaaS stack, including Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, and similar tools

 - Co-own Mac endpoint management through Rippling MDM, including configuration policies, OS and app patching, compliance enforcement, and device logistics for EMEA employees

 - Write Python and Bash automation for integrations and API work that falls outside Serval

 - Act as first responder for IT and access incidents during EMEA hours, judging when to resolve an issue yourself and when to escalate to the US team

 - Support security and compliance work, including MFA enforcement, audit-ready evidence for SOC 2, and data protection requirements for EMEA employees

 - Keep runbooks and the Serval knowledge base current so employees can find answers themselves and the US team can pick up your work at handoff

Your background looks something like this

 - 5–7 years of experience in IT systems, endpoint, or identity engineering, ideally at a fast-growing company

 - Hands-on administration experience with Okta

 - Working knowledge of SSO, SAML, OIDC, and SCIM

 - Experience managing SaaS platforms such as Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, Rippling, and Claude

 - Experience with Mac endpoint management (Rippling or similar MDM)

 - Automation you've shipped and can measure, whether scripts in Python or Bash or workflows in an iPaaS or ITSM platform, with results you can point to, such as ticket volume you eliminated

 - Experience as the sole or senior IT person at a site, comfortable making day-to-day decisions and knowing when a change needs sign-off

 - Strong async written communication, including clear handoffs, decision notes, and documentation as thorough as what you build

 - Strong troubleshooting instincts across systems that touch identity, networking, and SaaS integrations

 - Willingness to work in our London office 5 days a week

Even better if you have

 - Experience with Serval or another AI-native ITSM platform

 - Experience with iPaaS platforms like Workato, Zapier, or Tines

 - Exposure to AWS, GCP, or Azure administration

 - Familiarity with SOC 2, ISO 27001, or UK GDPR

 - Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform or similar)

 - Okta certifications

 - Experience supporting EMEA employees at a US-headquartered company

ABOUT E2B

E2B is a fast-growing Series A startup with over $37M in funding and 9-figure revenue. We are building the Agent Cloud and power the infrastructure behind AI labs and some of the most widely used consumer and enterprise agents, including Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, and Artificial Analysis. Our team includes original authors of Firecracker, the AWS microVM technology powering Lambda, along with alumni of Cognition, JetBrains, Zapier, and Wish.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Help E2B turn its data into clear, reliable insights that guide business decisions.

You'll own the business-facing layer of our data warehouse, including data models, metric definitions, forecasts, and reporting. You'll partner closely with our Head of Finance and expand that collaboration across E2B as the company grows. You'll sit within Engineering and work alongside a small but growing data team responsible for ingestion and the underlying platform.

Our stack is built on BigQuery and dbt. We prefer lightweight, code-first reporting, and you'll help shape how we build and deliver it.



Responsibilities include:

• Building and maintaining dbt models across usage, revenue, costs, margins, and customer data

• Establishing consistent definitions for core metrics, including revenue, usage, gross margin, churn, and expansion

• Reconciling product usage, invoiced revenue, and cash collections, and investigating discrepancies

• Creating reports, dashboards, and data apps that support Finance, company leadership, and the board

• Developing forecasts and models for revenue, usage growth, infrastructure costs, and the unit economics of new products


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

5+ years in analytics engineering, data analytics, or data science. We're more interested in what you've owned and delivered than your exact years of experience.

• Strong SQL skills: you're comfortable with window functions, choosing the right level of detail, and spotting results that don't hold up

• Financial understanding: you can distinguish billed, recognized, and collected revenue and investigate gaps between revenue, cash, and usage

• Experience with dbt or a comparable approach to building tested, version-controlled data models

• Strong Python skills for analysis and modeling, using tools such as pandas or polars and machine learning libraries

• Practical forecasting experience: you've built forecasts or financial models that informed real business decisions

• Thoughtful data visualization: your charts answer clear questions and communicate the limits of the underlying data

• A generalist approach: you can move comfortably between SQL, Python, reporting, and a working conversation with Finance

• End-to-end ownership: you identify gaps in reporting, define what's needed, build the solution, and maintain its accuracy

BONUS POINTS FOR:

• Experience building data apps with Streamlit, Evidence, Observable, Hex, or TypeScript/React

• Familiarity with GCP, AWS, or Azure, with a preference for GCP

• Experience setting up managed connectors such as Fivetran, Airbyte, or dlt to bring missing data into the warehouse

• Experience working at a startup or on a small team



At E2B, you'll have the freedom to shape your work and the responsibility to follow it through. We're looking for someone who takes initiative and owns the accuracy and usefulness of the numbers behind our decisions.




WHAT IT’S LIKE TO WORK AT E2B

We’re a fast-growing startup with offices in San Francisco and Prague, Czech Republic. We already generate 9-figure revenue and work directly with top-tier AI companies like Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, Artificial Analysis and other exciting teams pushing the frontier of AI.

We offer healthcare, vision, and dental insurance, unlimited PTO, 401k, and a variety of perks for in-office employees.

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - A fast learner who thrives in a fast-paced startup environment and asks for responsibility, not permission

 - English fluency

 - Legally authorized to work in the EU (for our Milan office) or the US (for our SF, NYC and Boston offices)

 - In your application, tell us the area where you'd have the most impact and show us the best thing you've ever made

 


BONUS POINTS FOR

 - You're a builder: you've won hackathons, ship side projects for fun, or are active in student organizations (tech clubs, robotics teams, startup societies, student media)

 - Something live in the world we can try: an app on the App Store or Play Store, a website, a product, a community, a publication (include the link in your application)

ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.


ABOUT THE ROLE

ElevenLabs is a voice AI company, and more and more startup founders and developers are building their products on our platform. We want to meet them in person and give them reasons to keep building with us.

We are looking for a Field Marketing Manager to own our events and field programs for startups and founders in the US. You will run our founder dinner series, a quarterly demo day in SF, and the happy hours, workshops and meetups that bring developers into the product. You will build Founder's Day Summit, a flagship event for about 100 founders, taking it from first idea to the day itself. You will also decide where we show up at other people's events, from AI conference sponsorships to side events and co-hosted programs with VCs, accelerators and partner brands.

This is a hands-on role. You will build guest lists, host the room, and work with ElevenLabs researchers, startup team members, the Grants program and VC partners to make each event worth a founder's evening. About two thirds of your events will be in San Francisco and one third in New York. You will measure what each event produces, whether that is sign-ups, activated accounts or pipeline, and use it to decide what to run next.

The right person knows the startup and AI scene in SF and New York, has a network of founders, VCs and builders, and has clear views on what makes an event worth attending. You will own a budget, juggle several partners at once, and run the events.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own a founder exec dinner series of 10 to 20 guests, sourcing founders through outbound and the Grants program and hosting with ElevenLabs researchers, startup team members and VC partners

ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE PEOPLE TEAM

 - Build the people function from scratch, fast enough to keep up with 10x growth. We grew headcount 10x in the last year and we're not slowing down. You'll build the systems, programs, and team from nothing, and make them work before we outgrow them.

 - Reinvent people operations around AI. Doing this by hand doesn't scale to a workforce growing this fast on a team this lean. You'll put AI at the core of how the function runs, so a small team supports many times its number.

 - Own the culture and comms as the company scales. When a company scales this quickly, staying connected and aligned doesn't happen on its own. You'll own the internal comms, events, and rhythm that keep a multi-site team that's growing fast bound to a shared culture.

 - Own day-to-day People support for managers and employees.  - Hold the company to federal, state and local employment regulations for a non-exempt workforce, finding and closing gaps before they become liabilities.

 - Build AI-powered tools and automation into HR workflows, experimenting with what creates leverage across the function and improving the systems that set employees up for success.

About us

Foundational is building the most precise picture of Earth and orbit, using lasers fired from the ground. We call it ground truth for orbit.

We design and run low-cost, autonomous satellite laser ranging stations. They measure the distance to satellites with extreme precision, day and night. Our data platform turns those measurements into tracking data and orbit products for satellite operators, space agencies and governments. We also build our own flight-proven laser retroreflector arrays, so any satellite can be tracked.

Our station network is expanding across continents. The data supports resilient navigation, Earth observation and the safe, sustainable use of space.

We're a small, fast-moving team of engineers, scientists and operators in London. We're backed by venture investors and supported by ESA, the UK Space Agency, Innovate UK.

This is Foundational.

Role Overview
As the Senior Product Manager for Account Integrity, you will make sure every account on HighLevel is authentic and uses the platform as intended. You will own the strategy and roadmap for preventing fake account creation, bots and fake traffic, SMS abuse, email abuse, affiliate and benefits abuse, and the handling of third-party abuse complaints.
 
Abuse on HighLevel shows up on many surfaces at once: signup, public forms, messaging, affiliates, funnels and websites, domains, and AI agents. You will build the detection layer, a shared definition of an abusive account, and the graduated enforcement system that stops abuse early while keeping friction off legitimate businesses.
 
You will set requirements and shared standards for integrity across the platform, and partner with the engineering teams that own each surface to build on work they already have in flight. Success in this role depends on strong cross-team leadership, crisp prioritization, and the ability to make a data-backed case for integrity work across many roadmaps.
This role sits on the Trust & Safety product team and shares a common detection, trust-scoring, and enforcement platform with the Account Security and Payment Risk verticals.
Key Responsibilities
Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Account Integrity across signup, forms, messaging, affiliates, hosting, domains, and AI features.
Define a shared definition of an abusive or inauthentic account, and drive the Account Integrity North Star along with its input and counter metrics.
Build signup and onboarding defenses: device, browser, and network fingerprinting, bot detection, velocity limits, and re-entry prevention for banned actors.
Drive controls that prevent messaging abuse and toll fraud, such as volume and destination limits and spend ceilings, in partnership with the messaging and product teams.
Define permission limits that unlock abusable capabilities, such as messaging at scale, payments, and payouts, as an account builds history and verifies who it is.
Own graduated enforcement capabilities with clear appeal paths and audit trails.
Build intake, routing, and SLAs for abuse and takedown reports.
Partner with Affiliates, Finance, and Payments to detect affiliate and benefits abuse before commissions and credits are paid.
Work with Support/CX on investigator tooling, playbooks, and the operational model for integrity reviews.
Run a weekly review of abuse caught and missed, false positives and appeals, time to takedown, and the dollar and customer cost of each.
Requirements
6+ years of Product Management experience, including significant ownership of trust & safety, fraud, abuse prevention, integrity, or risk products.
Experience building abuse detection, risk scoring, bot mitigation, or automated enforcement systems at scale.
Strong understanding of platform abuse patterns: fake accounts, bots, SMS pumping and toll fraud, phishing and credential harvesting, promotion and affiliate abuse.
Proven ability to lead through influence: driving priorities across engineering teams you do not manage.
Strong analytical skills: comfortable writing SQL, defining labels and metrics, and reasoning about precision, recall, and false positive cost.
Excellent written communication and stakeholder management across Engineering, Support, Legal, Finance, and senior leadership.
Nice-to-Have
Experience with onboarding or growth products.
Experience with abuse of generative AI products and agent safety controls.
Core KPIs
Volume of accounts showing abusive behavior with financial impact.
Reduction in fake signups and trials, SMS pumping volume and cost, and affiliate fraud losses.
Median time to enforce.
Share of abuse detected proactively rather than through customer, vendor, or third-party reports.
False positive rate, appeal overturn rate, and support tickets driven by enforcement.
Abuse report intake SLA and operational efficiency.

THE ROLE

Technical Program Managers (TPMs) exist to make cross functional and cross organizational work land. A TPM owns the outcome across teams that do not report to each other, holds the dependencies nobody else is holding, and makes progress visible without pushing reporting overhead onto the teams doing the work. TPMs are not just stenographers or status chasers, but end-to-end problem solvers from discovery -> execution. As a jack or jill of all traits, TPMs get the job done no matter the hurdles in their way.

As the Manufacturing Capabilities TPM, you will own what each new manufacturing capability needs from Hadrian's software, automation, and infrastructure teams, from a customer's requirements to qualified parts. Welding, casting, and sheet metal are examples. A capability is ready only when its equipment, its process, and its software are ready together, and each of those has a different owner. Your partners are the engineering leads for each capability, Quality, Factory Development, the Manufacturing Software teams, and the program managers who own the customer contracts. You will join a small TPM function that is still defining how it works. Customer contracts are the reason a capability gets built; you will be the reason the capabilities support future contracts with ease by approaching your work with a platform mindset.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Discovery: Start by finding out what each new capability needs from engineering. Some of it is known today and much of it is not, so the first deliverable is the map.

 - Capability standup: Own the engineering side of standing up a new capability. Work back from the customer's milestone and hold one plan across the software, automation, and infrastructure work it depends on.

 - Definition of ready: Decide with engineering and Quality what ready means for each capability, and write it down. Trace each customer requirement to the procedure, equipment, or software that meets it, so gaps show up early and not at qualification.

 - Needs across teams: Turn what a capability needs from software, infrastructure, and security into requirements those teams can plan against. You own the capability and the TPMs for those domains own their layers, so you work through them rather than around them.

 - Qualification: Hold the path from procedure development to qualification, so the people, the procedures, and the records are ready when the equipment is.

 - Capabilities across programs: Keep one view of where each capability stands at each site. When the next customer program needs a capability, start from what the last one built.

 - Function building: Help define what TPM means at Hadrian, leading by example.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 8+ years in technical program management or product management, at least 3 of them owning programs across engineering and operations teams that did not report to you.

 - Experience driving programs from 0 to 1. You are not just a facilitator, but a complete owner end to end.

 - Has defined what done means for something new. You wrote the requirements and acceptance criteria, and held them when a team called the work finished early.

 - Learns a technical domain quickly. You can sit with a weld engineer, a quality lead, and a software engineer in the same week and follow each of them.

 - Strong written communication favoring asynchronous updates over synchronous meetings.

 - Bachelor's degree in an engineering field, Computer Science, or equivalent experience.

 - Willingness to travel. New factories are being stood up, and time on the floor is necessary to understand what each capability needs.




WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

 - Knows how to uplevel themselves using AI without dumping slop on their stakeholders.

 - Knows how to bring efficiency over process for process' sake. Doing this requires a broad toolkit vs always bringing a hammer regardless of the problem context.

 - Time as a product manager, owning requirements and tradeoffs for a product other teams depended on.

 - Experience in manufacturing or hardware, where physical work and software had to be ready on the same day.

 - Experience in defense, aerospace, or another regulated field where a part does not ship until its process is qualified.

 - Technically fluent enough to influence design discussions in the domain, covering weld and inspection processes, quality systems such as AS9100, and the software that plans and tracks production.

 - Partner across Supply Chain, Capability Engineering, Production/Manufacturing Engineering, Software, Materials & Processes, Test, and Customer Programs/Forward Deployed Engineering to unblock constraints before they affect the build.

 - Represent Build Engineering in cross-functional planning, program reviews, and leadership and customer updates.

 - Assess build and manufacturability risk across the portfolio and drive mitigation plans to protect schedule and quality.

Role highlights

 - Role: Product Design Intern, ICEYE Intern Lab

 - Location: Espoo, Finland (onsite), potentially with some travel

 - Department: Product Management

 - Employment type: Fixed-term, fully paid internship (3-6 months, flexible)

WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT

Design for space. Yes, really.

Most design internships hand you a made-up brief and a tote bag. Ours is an apprenticeship: you learn the craft by working next to someone who's really good at it, on real projects, the way designers, typographers and architects always have.

 - One staff designer, all yours. You're paired one to one with a staff designer for the whole internship. Sit in on their crits, watch how they frame problems and make calls, and get line-by-line feedback on your work.

 - You bring the AI skills. We teach the rest. You can probably prototype faster than we could when we started. What takes longer is craft, judgment and taste: knowing which of your 50 options is the right one, and why. That's the curriculum.

 - It's real work. You're on the team with a live project, your own manager, and product managers, engineers and scientists down the hall. Customers use what you design to make decisions that matter.

 - Small on purpose. We take only a few interns, so nobody gets lost in the crowd.

 - It's paid. Fully. Every internship should be.

We'll be honest: it's demanding. Things move fast and you'll be stretched. At 90 days, you'll sit down with your manager and someone from our People team to talk about how it's going, and about a full-time role if one is open.

You'll leave with shipped work, a mentor in your corner and a far sharper eye for what good looks like.




WHO WE ARE

ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation, giving customers intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.




YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES

Most of your time, you're designing on a live project next to your mentor. The rest goes into practice on purpose: crits, craft sessions and lots of feedback.

How the apprenticeship works

 1. Watch and learn. Shadow your mentor and sit in on their crits. Learn how radar satellites work (no physics degree needed), meet the people who use our products and ship a few small fixes.

 2. Design side by side. Own a defined piece of a live project with your mentor next to you, from understanding the problem to a design that ships. Expect close reviews and plenty of "why did you do that?"

 3. Run with it. Lead your piece with your mentor coaching rather than steering, and show it at demo day.

Most weeks, you'll

 - Walk through your work with your mentor, decision by decision.

 - Talk to users and our own experts about how they work with satellite data, then turn what you learn into flows and interfaces.

 - Prototype quickly with AI tools and test ideas with real users.

 - Work with product managers and engineers from the problem to the shipped thing.

 - Show your work at weekly crit, and give feedback too.

 - Join craft sessions with senior designers on type, layout, data visualisation and interaction detail.

 - Keep a short decision log: what you chose, what you dropped and why.
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You don't need a design job on your CV. Curiosity, a portfolio that shows how you think and a habit of making things will do.

Must haves

 - You're in the third year of a Bachelor's or later, doing a Master's, or recently graduated. Design, HCI or interaction design is ideal; other backgrounds are welcome if your portfolio shows how you think.

 - A portfolio that shows your process, not just final screens. School work, side projects and unfinished experiments all count.

 - You use AI tools when you design, and you have opinions on where they help and where they don't.

 - An eye for layout, type and detail, and enough Figma (or similar) to get ideas out of your head.

 - Curiosity about how complicated things work, and no fear of asking engineers and scientists lots of questions.

 - You can explain why you made a design choice, and you're open to hearing it might be wrong.

 - Fluent English, written and spoken.

 - The right to work onsite in Finland: you're an EU/EEA citizen, or you can get a visa (we'll help).

Nice to have

 - Something data-heavy you've designed: a dashboard, a map, an analytics tool.

 - Prototyping in code, or things you've built with AI coding tools.

 - Some user research or usability testing, even scrappy.

 - A previous internship, freelance work or a startup project.

 - An interest in space, defence or other work where the stakes are real.

Ticked none of these? Apply anyway. That's what an apprenticeship is for.

You…

 - ask lots of questions, including the ones that feel obvious

 - would rather make the thing than talk about it

 - can hear tough feedback on Monday and bring better work on Wednesday

 - want to learn from people better than you, and one day be the one others learn from



WHAT ICEYE GIVES

 - A paid internship with a dedicated manager and a mentor

 - Live projects with real customer impact

 - Relocation support and work visa support, if needed.

 - A 90-day review and a conversation about full-time opportunities where there is an approved opening




RECRUITMENT PROCESS

Applications close on 20.12.2026. We review applications on a rolling basis, so apply early. The internship starts in April/May 2027.

 1. Application: Submit your CV, a link to your portfolio and answers to a few short questions instead of a cover letter (about 30 minutes).

 2. Peer conversation (30 min): A chat with an ICEYE PEER about how you work, learn and collaborate.

 3. Product Design team interview (60 min): A conversation with the Product Design team, including a walkthrough of one project from your portfolio and a short practical exercise. We care more about how you approach the problem than about getting a perfect answer.

 4. Decision and offer.

THE ROLE IN ONE LINE

Being an EM at incident.io http://incident.io isn't managing from above. You're close enough to the work to see trouble coming, you're in the room when it's hard, and your team makes better calls because you're there.


WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE DAY TO DAY

You'll lead a team of engineers who own their work end to end, from the first customer conversation to running it in production. There's no buffer role here. Our engineers talk to customers directly, and so will you. Your job isn't to stand between the team and the outside world, it's to clear the path so they can move. You'll pair closely with product manager, tech lead, and other managers.

You stay close enough to every project to know where it stands without asking for a status update. You notice drift early and spot the next bottleneck before the team is faced with it. You know the distinction between micro-managing and being micro-interested. When the team does get stuck, you ask "what would it take?", help them make the trade-off, then back their call with your peers and engineering leadership. We push to deliver as much value as we can, as fast as we can, and work finished beats work started, so you care about getting projects over the line, not just keeping them moving.

You hold the bar for everything your team ships, from the product to the comms that go to customers. We want teams so good that engineers elsewhere hear about them and want in. You own the outcomes, including who's on the team: if it needs different people, you go and find them.

Customers trust us when things go wrong. They depend on incident.io http://incident.io's resilience to know when their own systems are in trouble and to invest in making them better. That makes reliability part of everything your team ships, and when something does break on our side, you're in the room keeping things calm and making sure we come out of it stronger.

All of our teams are pushing the frontier of what's possible with AI. Investigations, our AI product, runs multi-agent analysis across historical incidents, telemetry systems, multiple datasources, including codebases, to find root cause in minutes. You'll understand these systems well enough to make your team's technical calls better: you challenge assumptions, question complexity nobody needs, and raise the trade-offs people missed. You don't need the best answer in the room, you need to improve the discussion and the outcomes.

This isn't a delivery manager role or a people-only one: we think an EM can run a team and still hold a high technical bar. And have fun too (check what one of our EMs built https://incident.io/careers/candidate-hub/product#how-you-fit/start for hiring).

The way we work changes often. You'll help shape it, bringing what you've seen work (and not work) elsewhere to improve how we build.


WHO YOU ARE

 - You've managed engineers before, and you came up as one. You might still believe deep down you are still one. You can sit through an architecture discussion, listen for most of it, then ask the one question that makes an engineer rethink their approach. You don't drive every technical decision, but the ones you're part of come out better, and you can explain why they matter to someone who'll never read the code.

 - You measure yourself by how much your people grow, not just what the team ships. You know where each engineer wants to go and find the work that gets them there. And you spot the quiet ones doing great work and make sure others see it too. In our team we call these “silent killers https://lnkd.in/p/eJ_fd9TU”.

 - When the team is on a bad day, your first move is to support them. Nobody does their best work feeling exposed, so you make sure people feel safe and supported, and you know what works best for each person.

 - You work out what drives each person and why they approach things the way they do, and that's what lets you challenge them and have the hard conversations without losing their trust. You care about your engineers and you also push them.

 - Feedback is a gift, as long as it’s well delivered. You give it often and directly, so nobody learns something new about themselves in a review, and you want it back, whether it comes from your manager, a peer or the newest engineer on the team.

 - When the team is stuck, you help them decide rather than deciding for them. Is this the right customer problem? Is the complexity worth it? Does the investment make sense for the business? Sometimes that means pushing back, sometimes that means giving voice to the quite person. In the end, you foster how the team gets to responsible outcomes and you hold the proper accountability.

 - You are biased towards action because you think actions speak louder than words. Obviously you are able to do so whilst being empathetic and managing your peers and stakeholders effectively.

 - You push back on leadership and other managers too. If leadership gets something wrong or our expectations are unclear, you tell us.

 - You've seen what good looks like elsewhere, and you adapt it to our culture rather than dropping it verbatim into our ways of working.

Full Stack Software Engineer, Lab Platform (LIMS)

THE OPPORTUNITY

insitro is a physical AI company dedicated to unlocking causal human biology and accelerating the delivery of better medicines to patients. Our unique Virtual Human™ platform identifies novel, high-impact genetic intervention points, which our TherML™ platform translates into therapeutics—whether small molecules, biologics, or oligos. With multiple programs in metabolic disease and neuroscience advancing toward the clinic, and our first IND submission slated for the second half of this year, we are at a pivotal inflection point.

To enable that mission, we need a software layer that ties together the scientific, automation, and machine learning platforms — that's our Lab Platform: a harness for science, built as an agentic workflow system that lets scientists drive the lab through an agent. Our bar is that everything in the lab should be agentically accessible (any action a scientist can take, an agent can take), agentically legible (agents understand what the data means in insitro's context, not just how to fetch it), and humanly verifiable (a scientist can always check what an agent did and why). This is real robotics, workflow automation, and applied agent tooling — and your users are in the building with you.

You'll work across the stack — front end, backend, and the integrations that reach into instruments, Benchling, and agent runtimes — partnering closely with our machine learning, automation, and biology teams. Based in South San Francisco, this role reports directly to Senior Manager, Software Engineering and offers an in-person hybrid schedule of three days per week. We'll bring you up to speed in the domain of drug development and back your ideas with real trust and mentorship along the way.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

Full-Stack Ownership

 - Ship Across the Stack: Build the React and TypeScript frontends scientists use every day, the Python services behind them, and integrations that reach instruments, Benchling, and agent runtimes

 - Own It End to End: Take a feature from the first conversation with a scientist through the data model and UI to the alert that fires when it breaks

 - Do the Normal SWE Things: Write code, review design docs, talk to users, and do code reviews that actually make the codebase better

Agentic Tooling & Experimentation

 - Chase User Appreciation: Ship things that make scientists say "OMG, this is amazing, thank you so much."

 - Figure Out What's Actually Useful: Test agentic tooling ideas through prototypes, real users, and short iterative loops rather than betting on theory

 - Move the Needle: Contribute work that meaningfully advances insitro's mission and the pace of drug development

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Go Watch the Work: Spend time in the lab observing the workflow before you change it

 - Partner Broadly: Collaborate closely with machine learning, automation, and biology teams to build tools people actually use

 - Keep Humans in the Loop: Design for provenance and verifiability, so a scientist can always check what an agent did and why

 


ABOUT YOU

Experience & Qualifications

 - Tenure: 2–4+ years of experience as a professional software engineer

 - Engineering Fundamentals: Working knowledge of AWS or GCP, relational databases, and standard practices like version control and code review

Core Competencies

 - Product Instinct: You think like a product person — you want to know who the user is, what they're actually trying to do, and you have opinions about what to build

 - Curious About the Science: You don't need a biology background, but you want to learn the domain rather than treat it as someone else's problem

By being humble, supportive, and truly giving a sh*t, the team ensures that our customers are successful in Jobber. This team thrives on meaningful and impactful communication with one another and with our customers and plays a significant role in the lives of entrepreneurs and business owners who utilize Jobber.



Our Onboarding team is a critical part of the customer journey, responsible for activation, retention, and depth of adoption. Onboarding ensures that Service Providers - from fast-growing home service businesses to our largest and most complex accounts - get a high-touch onboarding experience that removes friction from day one. The team partners closely with Sales, Product, R&D, Support, and Customer Success to align on launches, resolve blockers, and continuously strengthen the customer experience.



The role:

Reporting to the Director, Customer Onboarding, the Senior Manager, Customer Onboarding will lead the Onboarding Specialists and Managers who serve our largest, most complex and strategic accounts. This is a true ownership role: you are accountable for the service delivery, execution, and results of the Onboarding Managers and Specialists in your service model — and for the experience of every customer in your portfolio.



We're looking for a tenured leader who has done this before. Someone who builds trust across the business quickly, goes deep enough on our product to be credible in the room with our biggest customers, communicates like an executive, and defaults to action when things are ambiguous (and they will be — we move fast!).



The Senior Manager, Customer Onboarding will:

 - Own the service delivery and execution of your portfolio. You are accountable for the performance of the Onboarding Managers and Specialists in your segment, and for the experience and outcomes of every customer in it. When something is off track, you drive it to resolution.

 - Manage and develop a team of Onboarding Managers and Onboarding Specialists — and build coaches, not just a team. Your Managers are coaches first: you’ll develop their coaching craft, hold the standard on QA and coaching cadences, and treat the performance of every IC in your org as a reflection of the leadership environment above them. You optimize results through effective performance management — 1:1’s, “real-time” coaching, documented career plans, feedback that flows both ways, and any other creative programs you think will be impactful. In order to be successful, our employees need to clearly understand how to get there — and when someone isn’t meeting the bar, you address it early and with care. Underperformance never lingers on your team. You build systems and standards that hold without you in the room.

 - Own it end-to-end, and default to action. Leaders who thrive here pressure-test ideas, then commit fully, champion them with their team, and see them through when the work gets messy. You don’t wait for context to find you - you go get it. When you’re unclear, blocked, or unaligned, you raise it early and directly, make the call with the information you have, and close your own loops.

 - Bring solutions, not status. You show up to leadership conversations with the problem framed, the data decision-ready, and a recommendation on the table. You stand behind your numbers - and if the data isn't ready to act on, you say so and own getting it there.

 - Know the business. You understand how your portfolio’s performance connects to the broader business, you proactively spot opportunities and risks before they show up in a dashboard - and you bring leadership a recommended solution, then mobilize your team to execute on it

 - Go deep on the product. Our biggest customers run complex operations, and their onboarding gets technical. You'll become an expert in Jobber - enough to guide tough conversations about workflows, integrations, data, and rollout plans with confidence and credibility, supporting the team during high impact projects as needed.

 - Drive execution excellence through tooling - including AI. You’ll optimize Salesforce and our platform stack, and lead your team’s adoption of AI-enabled workflows: knowing when to trust them, when to verify, and how to feed what your team learns back into the system.

 - Bring executive presence. You’ll represent your portfolio and service model with Jobber’s leadership, and represent Jobber with the senior stakeholders at our largest customers - communicating with clarity and composure, especially when things aren't going as expected.

 - Build strong cross-functional relationships across Sales, Support, Product, Marketing, Analytics, Enablement and Partnerships, so your team can provide informed, proactive support in accordance with all campaigns, product launches and customer initiatives.

 - Recruit, onboard and ramp new hires quickly - and feed what’s working back to Enablement so training gets better for everyone.”

 - Become an ambassador of our culture by being humble, supportive, and someone who truly gives a shit!


TO BE SUCCESSFUL, YOU'LL NEED:

 - 5+ years in post-sale SaaS customer success or onboarding, including several years leading teams - and you understand the difference between managing a team and building leaders who run their own. Experience managing managers is strongly preferred.

 - Hands-on experience managing Key/Large Account think enterprise-grade or multi-location customers, complex rollouts, and multiple senior stakeholders on both sides of the table.

 - A track record of true end-to-end ownership: you've been accountable for the outcomes of a portfolio, not just the activities of a team.

 - Strong business acumen for your scope: you’re fluent in the metrics that drive your service model, you understand how your team’s performance ladders up to the business, and when you spot an opportunity you come to leadership with a recommended solution - not just the problem.

 - Next level communication and relationship building abilities. We move fast, which means you'll need to build a high degree of trust with peers and key stakeholders — and the executive presence to articulate strategic ideas with leadership and deliver on high-level concepts.

 - A strong understanding of Salesforce, spreadsheets, and any other methodology of getting the data you need - you build your own view of performance rather than waiting for it to be handed to you.

 - To be agile and adaptable in a very fast-paced environment. We're growing fast and things are changing every day - what worked yesterday might not anymore. You need to be invigorated by this type of environment, and be excited by a new challenge.

 - An incredible passion for our customer and a connection to our purpose — to help small and commercial businesses be more successful.
