ARE YOU PASSIONATE ABOUT HELPING CUSTOMERS SUCCEED, SOLVING MEANINGFUL PROBLEMS, AND MAKING A REAL IMPACT ON THE BUSINESSES YOU SUPPORT EVERY DAY?

We’re looking for a Retention Specialist to join our Customer Success team and play a key role in helping customers overcome challenges, rediscover the value of Jobber, and continue growing their businesses with confidence.

The Team:

The Retention team plays a critical role in protecting recurring revenue and strengthening long-term customer relationships, supporting customers at pivotal moments when they are deciding whether to continue their Jobber subscription.

Through both inbound and outbound retention conversations, our team connects with customers who may be experiencing challenges, exploring alternatives, or not yet seeing the full value of the platform. We take the time to understand what’s getting in the way, and then connect them to the Jobber features and workflows that solve their specific problems and help their businesses grow.

We partner closely with Customer Success, Support, Product, and Billing to surface churn risks, share insights from customer conversations, and continuously improve the overall customer experience.



The Role:

Reporting to the Manager, Customer Retention, the Retention Specialist works directly with customers who may be at risk of cancelling or disengaging from Jobber. Your job is to understand what’s standing in their way, and connect them to solutions that help them succeed.

You’ll lead meaningful, consultative conversations to understand the underlying causes behind cancellation requests or disengagement, identify barriers to success, and guide customers toward solutions that strengthen their experience with Jobber and make a real difference for their business. You’ll ask the right questions before offering solutions, and you’ll treat every conversation as an opportunity to genuinely improve someone’s experience.

Retention Specialists engage with customers through inbound calls, proactive retention outreach, and scheduled value sessions, translating Jobber’s capabilities into practical, meaningful solutions tailored to each customer’s unique situation.

You’ll develop deep product knowledge and act as a trusted advisor to customers, confidently navigating complex conversations and leveraging your expertise to showcase how Jobber’s features solve meaningful problems for businesses, helping customers make informed decisions that drive their long-term success.

Success in this role is measured through outcomes such as save rate, customer retention, and long-term customer success following retention conversations, with Retention Specialists taking direct ownership of outcomes that impact recurring revenue retention.



Shift: Monday to Friday 11am to 8pm MT (12pm to 9pm ET)



Please note: This role is available only to candidates based in Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo and requires you to attend the office at least 1 day per week according to the department schedule

The Retention Specialist will:

 - Engage with customers at risk of cancellation through retention-focused phone conversations via direct inbound phone line or booked calls, identifying solutions that help them continue to succeed with Jobber.

 - Conduct proactive outbound retention calls to customers showing signs of churn risk, using available signals such as account health indicators or changes in engagement to help customers address challenges before they lead to cancellation.

 - Facilitate scheduled value sessions that help customers overcome blockers and unlock the full value of their Jobber subscription through feature adoption, workflow optimization, training, and best practices tailored to their business.

 - Use a consultative, diagnostic approach to uncover root causes behind churn risk. You’ll ask the right questions,  interpret signals such as product usage patterns and account health indicators, and recommend solutions that genuinely address what’s getting in the customer’s way.

 - Play a direct role in protecting and retaining recurring revenue by influencing customer decisions at critical moments in their lifecycle, guiding at-risk customers toward solutions that reinforce the long-term value of their Jobber subscription.

 - Exercise sound judgment and decision-making in navigating complex or high-risk customer situations, balancing customer needs with business outcomes to drive the best possible retention result.

 - Partner with cross-functional teams to share insights from retention conversations, helping identify churn trends, surface product gaps, and contribute to improvements across the customer experience.

 - Contribute to improving long-term retention strategy by identifying patterns in churn drivers and influencing cross-functional improvements to product, onboarding, and customer experience.

 - Adapt quickly to evolving processes, tools, and product updates in a growing environment where customer needs and solutions continue to evolve.

 - Become an ambassador of our culture by being humble, supportive – and someone who truly gives a shit!



To be successful, you should have:

 - A track record of thriving in high-volume, customer-facing environments where you consistently deliver strong results while maintaining a high-quality customer experience.

 - A genuine curiosity about what’s driving customer challenges. You ask great questions, listen closely, and understand the problem before proposing a solution.

 - The ability to translate product knowledge into customer solutions. You don’t just know what Jobber does – you can connect its features to the specific needs of each customer’s business in a way that resonates.

 - The ability to influence outcomes through consultative conversations, confidently guiding customers through complex situations such as cancellation decisions, product challenges, or pricing concerns.

 - Strong verbal communication skills and a customer-first mindset, allowing you to build rapport quickly and navigate challenging conversations with empathy and clarity.

 - A results-driven mindset that motivates you to take ownership of customer outcomes and work toward solutions that support long-term customer success.

 - Resilience and composure. You stay calm under pressure, handle rejection professionally, and learn quickly from difficult conversations.

 - Strong problem-solving ability. You assess situations critically, identify root causes, and propose creative, practical solutions with confidence.

 - Adaptability in a growth environment. You’re energized by change and comfortable learning new tools, systems, and workflows.

 - Reliability and accountability. You show up for your team and customers, follow through on commitments, and take responsibility for results.

 - Confidence working with modern software tools and navigating multiple systems in a fast-paced, cloud-based environment.

 - Interest or experience in leveraging AI tools to enhance productivity and insight generation.

WHAT IS KALSHI?

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

 - Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

 - Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

About the Role
You will work closely with engineering and product teams to embed security into the development lifecycle, proactively identify vulnerabilities, and build scalable security solutions that allow Kalshi to move quickly without compromising the integrity of our platform.

What You’ll Do

 - Develop reusable security components and frameworks that strengthen the security of our products and infrastructure.

 - Design and implement platform-wide security controls that proactively mitigate common vulnerabilities and emerging threats.

 - Identify, prioritize, and remediate security vulnerabilities across our technology stack.

 - Collaborate with engineering teams to investigate and address findings from internal security assessments, penetration testing, and external vulnerability reports.

 - Partner with product and engineering teams throughout the development lifecycle to ensure new products and features are secure by design.

 - Build and integrate automated security tooling that enables engineers to identify vulnerabilities earlier and ship secure software with confidence.


What You Need

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience.

 - 2+ years of experience in application security, product security, platform engineering, and/or infrastructure security.

 - Strong understanding of application security principles, common vulnerabilities, and mitigation techniques.

 - Ability to translate complex security and business requirements into practical, scalable engineering solutions.

 - Desire to work in a fast-paced, high-growth environment alongside exceptional engineers.


Nice to Haves

 - Experience building and securing cloud-native applications and distributed systems.

 - Experience with AWS and implementing security controls across cloud infrastructure.

 - Experience with automated security tooling, static analysis, vulnerability detection, and threat modeling.

 - Experience securing financial platforms, exchanges, trading systems, or other high-throughput, security-critical applications.

 - Experience working in a highly regulated environment.

As a Surveillance Analyst, you will help maintain the integrity of Kalshi’s markets by monitoring trading activity, investigating anomalies, and supporting the evolution of our surveillance framework. You will quickly develop a strong understanding of Kalshi’s products, market structure, and regulatory environment, taking ownership of investigations and producing clear, high-quality analysis for internal and regulatory stakeholders. WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Market Monitoring: Monitor real-time trading activity across Kalshi’s markets using surveillance tools and data analytics

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Agrotechnical Director based in Switzerland. As Agrotechnical Director, you will lead the agronomic vision and technical development of an innovative AI-powered agricultural technology platform. You will serve as the senior authority on agronomy, crop protection, and grower needs, ensuring that product development addresses real-world agricultural challenges and delivers measurable value. Working at the intersection of agriculture, technology, and business, you will guide decisions on crop priorities, pest detection, and innovative growing solutions. You will collaborate closely with Product, Sales, Operations, and Machine Learning teams to translate agricultural expertise into practical technological capabilities. You will also build strategic relationships with growers, industry associations, and agricultural partners across international markets. This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of precision agriculture while improving crop protection, reducing losses, and supporting more sustainable farming practices.
  • Lead Agrotechnical Strategy: Define and own the agronomic development strategy, identifying which crops, pests, growing systems, and technical capabilities should be prioritised. Cover different agricultural environments, including greenhouses, nurseries, propagation facilities, and outdoor cultivation.
  • Identify Customer Needs and Market Opportunities: Act as the internal authority on growers' challenges, operational priorities, and economic needs. Identify where agricultural businesses experience the greatest losses and costs, and determine which solutions offer the strongest commercial value.
  • Support Product and Commercial Strategy: Advise Product and Sales leadership by validating new ideas against real-world growing practices, identifying high-potential customer segments, and assessing the relevance of specific crops and use cases.
  • Develop Economic Value Propositions: Translate greenhouse and agricultural economics, including yields, labour, crop-protection expenses, energy costs, and crop-loss impacts, into measurable customer value propositions and return-on-investment (ROI) arguments.
  • Ensure Agronomic Quality: Own the agronomic methodology and content behind the digital crop-monitoring platform, including detection thresholds, recommended actions, pest and disease databases, and treatment guidance.
  • Collaborate on AI and Detection Models: Work closely with Machine Learning specialists to establish ground-truth data and labelling standards, validate detection models, and approve new pest and disease detection capabilities.
  • Lead Pilot Projects and Validation: Define agronomic pilot methodologies and success criteria, evaluate trial results, and develop case studies demonstrating measurable customer benefits and commercial potential.
  • Build Strategic Grower Relationships: Act as a senior agronomic advisor to strategic customers, maintaining relationships with head growers, Integrated Pest Management (IPM) managers, agronomists, and agrotechnical specialists.
  • Support Business Development: Participate in sales meetings when agronomic expertise is required, helping communicate technical value, address customer concerns, and demonstrate the practical benefits of agricultural technology solutions.
  • Develop Industry Partnerships: Build and strengthen relationships with grower cooperatives, agricultural associations, biological-control providers, and crop-protection companies. Represent the organisation at relevant industry events and professional gatherings.
  • Develop Agronomic Training: Design and deliver training programmes for customers and customer-facing teams, ensuring consistent understanding of agronomic methodologies and product capabilities.
  • Build and Lead the Agronomy Function: Establish, develop, and manage the agronomy team, fostering technical expertise, collaboration, and high-quality delivery.
  • Collaborate Cross-functionally: Work closely with senior management, Product, Sales, Operations, Machine Learning, and Engineering teams to ensure agronomic priorities are reflected in product development, customer delivery, and business strategy.
  • Measure Impact: Ensure that product and commercial priorities are supported by agronomic and economic evidence, that detection results are trusted by growers, and that pilots demonstrate measurable improvements such as earlier pest detection, reduced crop losses, optimised treatments, and lower scouting labour costs.

    • Requirements:

  • A bachelor's or master's degree in Agronomy, Horticulture, Plant Protection, or another relevant agricultural or agrotechnical discipline.
  • Extensive hands-on experience in commercial greenhouse production and outdoor cultivation, including crop scouting, Integrated Pest Management (IPM), and biological and chemical crop-protection methods.
  • Strong expertise in at least one of the following crops: tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, or medical cannabis.
  • Solid understanding of greenhouse and agricultural economics, including production costs, yield and margin drivers, labour requirements, and the financial consequences of crop losses.
  • Established professional relationships with grower cooperatives and agricultural associations in international markets, particularly the Netherlands and Canada.
  • Previous experience in AgTech or technology-driven agronomy, including field trials, pilot programmes, or the introduction of innovative agricultural solutions.
  • Proven ability to translate agronomic knowledge into commercially relevant recommendations, product requirements, and measurable customer value.
  • Strong professional credibility with head growers, IPM managers, agronomists, and senior agricultural stakeholders.
  • Previous leadership experience managing agronomists, technical specialists, or multidisciplinary agricultural teams.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain complex agronomic concepts to both technical and commercial audiences.
  • Fluent professional English, with the ability to collaborate effectively in an international working environment.
  • Knowledge of nurseries, propagation systems, and specialised growing environments is an advantage.
  • Familiarity with computer vision, automated crop scouting, or AI-powered agricultural technologies is highly desirable.
  • Experience collaborating with Machine Learning engineers or technology teams on data validation, detection models, and technical product development is a plus.
  • Previous experience working for a biological-control provider, crop-protection company, or seed business is considered an advantage.
  • An established professional reputation or visible presence within the horticulture and IPM community is highly valued.
  • Dutch language skills are an additional advantage.

    • Benefits:

  • International Exposure: Work with agricultural customers, growers, and industry partners across multiple international markets, including Europe and North America.
  • Strategic Influence: Take ownership of the agronomic direction and directly influence product development, commercial priorities, and customer value.
  • Innovation: Contribute to the development of advanced agricultural technologies combining computer vision, artificial intelligence, and agronomic expertise.
  • Leadership Opportunity: Build and lead the agronomy function while shaping its long-term strategy and development.
  • Meaningful Impact: Help commercial growers detect plant diseases and pests earlier, reduce crop losses, optimise treatments, and improve agricultural productivity.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Work alongside experienced professionals in Product, Sales, Operations, Machine Learning, and Engineering.
  • Professional Development: Expand your expertise at the intersection of agronomy, AI, and technology-driven agriculture.
  • Remote Working: Fully remote working arrangement.
  • Employment Type: Full-time.

  • Own and exceed individual revenue, bookings, gross margin, and pipeline targets across an assigned portfolio of enterprise accounts.

Director of Biomedical Equipment Services & Management

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Biomedical Equipment Services & Management based in the United States. The Director of Biomedical Equipment Services & Management will provide strategic leadership for medical equipment operations across an international network of hospitals. This role oversees the full equipment lifecycle, from planning and procurement to installation, maintenance, replacement, and retirement. You will lead technical teams, establish consistent standards, and strengthen equipment availability, safety, and long-term sustainability. Working closely with hospital leaders and cross-functional partners, you will guide capital planning, budgeting, training, and performance management. You will also oversee external technical partnerships and ensure that medical technologies remain appropriate for clinical needs and local operating environments. This is a senior leadership opportunity for an experienced healthcare technology professional who wants to improve the reliability of essential medical services across diverse, resource-constrained settings.

The Director will lead the development and execution of a coordinated biomedical equipment strategy, ensuring consistent standards, strong technical capabilities, and reliable equipment performance across the hospital network. The position is primarily focused on leadership, systems, and operational management rather than hands-on equipment repairs.

  • Lead biomedical teams and network performance: Manage and develop the central biomedical team, establish staffing models and performance expectations, set priorities, and oversee network-wide performance through KPI dashboards and regular reviews with senior leadership.

  • Oversee equipment lifecycle management: Develop and maintain a rolling three-to-five-year equipment replacement plan, establishing criteria for repair, replacement, redeployment, and retirement based on equipment condition, utilization, cost, and clinical requirements.

  • Ensure critical equipment availability: Monitor equipment uptime, downtime, and repair turnaround times. Establish appropriate backup equipment, spare-parts availability, service arrangements, and contingency plans to minimize disruptions to clinical services.

  • Guide equipment purchasing decisions: Review major equipment purchases and repairs through established capital planning processes, ensuring that investments meet clinical requirements and long-term operational needs.

  • Develop training and technical competencies: Lead the network-wide biomedical training strategy, establish role-based competency standards, and coordinate training in preventive and corrective maintenance, safety testing, and equipment-specific procedures.

  • Strengthen equipment standards: Maintain the standard medical-equipment list and guide equipment selection to ensure clinical suitability, technical supportability, and long-term sustainability. Evaluate new technologies and review exceptions in collaboration with medical leadership.

  • Assess donated equipment: Establish acceptance criteria and evaluate proposed equipment donations to determine whether they are appropriate, safe, and supportable.

  • Support capital projects and infrastructure: Lead the biomedical equipment workstream and collaborate with facilities, capital projects, clinical teams, and technical partners to align equipment plans with infrastructure requirements, lifecycle costs, and maintenance needs.

  • Oversee budgets and procurement: Develop and manage the central biomedical operating budget, contribute to long-term capital planning, define technical procurement requirements, approve standard purchases within delegated authority, and recommend larger investments through established approval processes.

  • Establish quality and safety standards: Develop policies for equipment commissioning, preventive and corrective maintenance, calibration, safety testing, recalls, decommissioning, and the investigation of equipment-related safety incidents.

  • Manage external technical partnerships: Oversee relationships with specialized service providers, coordinating technical support, equipment evaluations, training, major projects, and complex repair services.

  • Address medical-device technology risks: Work with IT teams on medical-device cybersecurity, software lifecycle management, and related technical risks.

  • Provide technical oversight of medical infrastructure: Guide biomedical infrastructure requirements, including medical-gas systems, in coordination with qualified external specialists.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate brings substantial experience in biomedical equipment services, clinical engineering, or healthcare technology management, together with a proven ability to lead technical teams and manage complex equipment portfolios. They should combine technical expertise with strategic planning, financial oversight, and strong cross-cultural collaboration skills.

  • Bachelor's degree in Biomedical Engineering, Clinical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

  • At least 7 years of progressively responsible experience in biomedical equipment services, clinical engineering, or healthcare technology management.

  • At least 5 years of leadership or supervisory experience managing biomedical, clinical engineering, or other technical teams.

  • Demonstrated experience managing medical-equipment lifecycles, replacement planning, equipment standardization, and major capital projects.

  • Experience designing and delivering technical training programs and establishing competency standards for biomedical personnel.

  • Strong knowledge of preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, equipment safety testing, and performance monitoring.

  • Experience using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) or similar software to manage equipment maintenance and performance.

  • Proven ability to develop and manage operating and capital budgets.

  • Experience overseeing external service providers, technical partners, and equipment vendors.

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify operational risks and implement sustainable improvements.

  • Effective communication and collaboration skills, particularly when working with hospital leadership, clinical teams, procurement, facilities, finance, and IT.

  • Sound judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities across a geographically distributed organization.

  • Professional certification such as Certified Biomedical Equipment Technician (CBET) or Certified Clinical Engineer (CCE) is preferred.

  • Experience working in international, multicultural, or resource-constrained healthcare environments is an advantage.

  • Willingness and ability to travel internationally, with travel expected to reach up to 25%.

  • Agreement with the declarations outlined in the partner organization's Statement of Faith is required.

    • Benefits:

  • Full-time, remote position.

  • Ideally based on the continent of Africa, in one of the countries where the hospital network operates.

  • Up to 25% travel.

  • Opportunity to lead biomedical equipment strategy across an international healthcare network.

  • Significant scope to strengthen medical equipment reliability, safety, and sustainability.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Customer Success (Legal) based in New York. As Director of Customer Success, you will lead the Americas Customer Success organization, driving customer adoption, engagement, retention, and long-term business growth within the legal technology sector. You will manage and develop a high-performing team while building trusted relationships with senior customer stakeholders. Your focus will be on ensuring customers successfully adopt and maximize the value of enterprise software solutions, including AI-powered capabilities. Working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Implementation, and Support, you will drive proactive account management and operational excellence. You will also oversee customer health, resolve escalations, and translate customer insights into opportunities for improvement and expansion. This is a strategic leadership opportunity within a global SaaS environment focused on innovation, collaboration, and measurable customer impact.

Lead the regional Customer Success strategy and ensure customers achieve meaningful value from their technology investments. Develop a proactive, customer-focused organization that drives product awareness, adoption, activation, satisfaction, and retention while supporting commercial growth.

  • Lead the Americas Customer Success team, establishing regional strategies, team objectives, and individual performance goals in partnership with senior leadership.

  • Coach, mentor, and develop Customer Success Managers, supporting their professional growth, product knowledge, and performance.

  • Oversee recruitment, onboarding, talent development, and performance management to build a high-performing team.

  • Drive customer awareness, product adoption, and activation through targeted initiatives, adoption reviews, and customer-specific roadmaps.

  • Ensure customers understand their product capabilities, successfully deploy solutions across their organizations, and achieve consistent usage.

  • Guide the team in delivering proactive customer engagement, onboarding, user training, and adoption programs in collaboration with Implementation, Training, and Support teams.

  • Lead team upskilling initiatives covering core products, AI functionality, and new product features.

  • Monitor customer health scores, product usage data, and Voice of the Customer insights to identify at-risk accounts and address potential issues early.

  • Lead root cause analysis, manage regional escalations, and coordinate cross-functional solutions to resolve complex customer challenges.

  • Own end-to-end customer delivery and serve as a key escalation point for Sales and other internal stakeholders.

  • Partner with Renewals, Risk, Sales, and Account Executive teams to achieve renewal and net revenue retention (NRR) targets.

  • Identify opportunities to reduce churn, recover at-risk accounts, and generate expansion opportunities through customer adoption insights.

  • Define, monitor, and report key performance indicators covering awareness, adoption, activation, renewals, and customer satisfaction.

  • Maintain structured performance reporting through established Customer Success operating processes.

  • Collaborate with Sales leadership on pipeline reviews, joint account planning, and go-to-market strategies.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Marketing teams to communicate customer feedback, influence product improvements, and support customer advocacy initiatives.

  • Organize executive briefings, customer events, and user groups to strengthen relationships and encourage engagement.

  • Monitor competitive developments, regulatory changes, and regional market trends, ensuring customer strategies reflect local business and legal requirements.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is an experienced Customer Success leader with a strong background in enterprise software, technology, or professional services. You should have a proven ability to build and develop teams, manage complex customer relationships, and drive measurable improvements in adoption and retention. Strong commercial awareness, executive communication skills, and a proactive approach to problem-solving are essential.

  • 7+ years of experience leading Customer Success, customer training, adoption, support, or operations teams within a software, technology, or professional services environment.

  • Demonstrated success improving customer adoption, activation, retention, and overall satisfaction.

  • Proven experience building, coaching, developing, and holding teams accountable, including hiring and performance management responsibilities.

  • Ability to influence Sales leaders and cross-functional stakeholders without relying on direct reporting relationships.

  • Experience driving customer adoption through training, enablement, change management, or structured engagement programs.

  • Track record of transforming reactive customer service teams into proactive Customer Success organizations.

  • Ability to quickly develop strong product knowledge and explain software functionality and business value to both end users and IT leaders.

  • Experience identifying at-risk accounts, managing escalations, conducting root cause analysis, and implementing customer recovery strategies.

  • Strong executive presence and ability to establish trusted relationships with customer IT leaders and senior decision-makers.

  • Understanding of SaaS business models and key performance indicators, including renewals, retention, adoption, and net revenue retention.

  • Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.

  • Strong business acumen, emotional intelligence, and ability to balance customer empathy with accountability and performance expectations.

    • Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in legal technology, law firms, or corporate legal environments, including leadership roles in IT operations, help desk, or user training.

  • Familiarity with legal industry buyers, regional regulatory requirements, and market developments.

  • Previous Customer Success leadership experience within a software or SaaS organization.

  • Working knowledge of legal technology and document management solutions, particularly iManage Work, Drive, Tracker, and Insight+.

  • Understanding of SaaS and cloud technologies, with the ability to connect product capabilities to customer use cases and business outcomes.

  • Experience managing channel or technology partners as extensions of a Customer Success organization.

  • Hands-on experience with Customer Success platforms, Salesforce, and customer support or ticketing systems.

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) or ITIL certification.

  • Annual performance-based bonus.

  • Comprehensive health, vision, dental, and life insurance coverage.

  • Multiple company wellness days throughout the year.

  • Access to RethinkCare, a global behavioral health and well-being platform offering resources for personal resilience and parental support.

  • Flexible working hours and remote work opportunities.

  • Occasional travel for local office collaboration, company events, team-building activities, and strategic meetings.

  • Unlimited access to LinkedIn Learning and interactive Microsoft courses and training.

  • Opportunities to pursue professional certifications and develop new skills.

  • Internal career development framework supporting long-term professional growth.

  • Inclusive and collaborative international working environment.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Finance & Operations based in the United States. The Director of Finance & Operations will lead the financial infrastructure and operational systems of a mission-driven organization investing in solutions that improve animal welfare in agriculture and aquaculture. This is a hands-on leadership role combining nonprofit finance, venture investment administration, and startup operations. You will oversee accounting, budgeting, cash management, funder reporting, and investment closings while ensuring strong financial controls and compliance. You will also help launch and support new companies, building the operational foundations they need to grow. Working closely with the CEO, external advisors, legal counsel, and portfolio teams, you will shape scalable processes across a diverse organization. This is an opportunity to take ownership of a broad operational scope and ensure that philanthropic capital is deployed efficiently, responsibly, and with measurable impact.

The Director of Finance & Operations will establish and manage the financial, investment, and operational systems that support the organization and its portfolio. The role requires both strategic oversight and hands-on execution across several interconnected areas.

  • Lead financial management: Oversee accounting, budgeting, monthly closing, bill payments, and payroll. Determine which finance activities should remain outsourced and which should be managed internally.

  • Manage restricted funding: Track multiple restricted grants, prepare budget-versus-actual reports and funder updates, maintain audit readiness, and coordinate annual tax filings and Form 990 preparation with external accountants.

  • Oversee cash flow and financial controls: Develop annual budgets, forecast cash requirements, manage treasury activities, and implement robust payment approval and wire-verification procedures.

  • Support financial planning and modeling: Help incubated companies and investment teams develop and evaluate five-year financial models, challenging assumptions and identifying financial risks.

  • Manage investment closings: Coordinate with legal counsel on equity investments, loans, and grants, overseeing documentation, signatures, fund transfers, and capitalization records.

  • Administer portfolio investments: Maintain capitalization tables and board-compliance calendars, and collect and report quarterly financial and animal-welfare metrics from portfolio companies.

  • Coordinate investment diligence: Organize data rooms, manage financial due diligence checklists, and review relevant company documentation.

  • Support new company launches: Help newly established companies set up their legal entities, banking, accounting, payroll, and insurance arrangements. Coordinate ongoing support with external finance and HR partners and assist with government and foundation grant applications.

  • Coordinate legal and contractual matters: Work with external counsel on charitable-purpose documentation, investment agreements, intellectual property assignments and licenses, and commercial contracts.

  • Manage organizational operations: Oversee Google Workspace, devices, access permissions, security practices, and website administration for the organization and new companies until they can manage these independently.

  • Oversee people and workplace operations: Support onboarding and offboarding, manage contractors, coordinate insurance coverage, and oversee leases and vendor contracts for offices and engineering facilities.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is an experienced finance and operations professional who combines strong accounting fundamentals with investment administration experience and the ability to build reliable systems in a growing organization. You should be comfortable taking ownership, working independently, and navigating a fast-changing environment.

  • At least 5 years of experience in finance and operations, including experience as the senior finance or operations professional within an organization.

  • Background in a foundation, venture capital fund, family office, or early-stage startup is strongly preferred.

  • Strong hands-on accounting skills, including managing monthly closes, reconciling accounts, and maintaining restricted-grant ledgers.

  • Experience with nonprofit fund accounting is an advantage.

  • Exposure to investment closings through fund operations, venture capital administration, or startup finance, including capitalization tables and investor reporting.

  • Ability to build financial models and critically assess financial assumptions, forecasts, and business plans.

  • Demonstrated ability to design and improve operational processes, systems, and controls rather than simply maintain existing workflows.

  • Familiarity with AI and automation tools and a willingness to incorporate them into daily work.

  • Legal and contract-related experience is a strong plus.

  • Sound judgment, discretion, and integrity when handling confidential financial information and investment-related matters.

  • Strong problem-solving skills, self-motivation, and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

  • Genuine interest in the mission of improving animal welfare through innovative products and investments.

    • Relevant backgrounds may include financial controllers or finance and operations leaders at small impact funds, fund operations professionals at early-stage venture firms, finance and operations leaders at seed-to-Series A startups, or professionals who have transitioned from audit or advisory roles into in-house finance leadership.

  • Half-time compensation of $80,000–$90,000 annually.

  • Full-time compensation of $160,000–$180,000 annually.

  • Benefits included, with specific details to be discussed during the hiring process.

  • Flexible working arrangement, with the option to work remotely or from an office in the San Francisco Bay Area.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Financial Planning & Analysis based in the United States. The Director of Financial Planning & Analysis will establish and lead a dedicated FP&A function, overseeing financial planning, forecasting, modeling, and performance analytics across multiple business operations. Reporting to the CFO, this hands-on leadership role will serve as a strategic partner to executive leadership and teams across Marketing, Accounting, Supply Chain, and Operations. You will develop sophisticated financial models, establish performance metrics, and translate complex financial and operational data into actionable business recommendations. The Director will take ownership of company-wide financial planning and performance management, building the processes, systems, and team capabilities needed to support sustainable growth and informed executive decision-making.

  • Financial Planning and Forecasting

  • Lead the annual operating plan and budgeting process across all departments.

  • Design and manage rolling monthly forecasts covering revenue, margins, operating expenses, EBITDA, cash flow, and cohort performance.

  • Develop and maintain the company's three-statement financial model and long-range financial plan.

  • Transition ownership of company-wide forecasting from an external consultant while improving budgeting and forecasting processes across departments.

  • Financial Analysis and Decision Support

  • Partner with department leaders to evaluate financial and operational performance, identify key business drivers, and recommend actions aligned with organizational objectives.

  • Analyze product and channel unit economics, including gross margins, contribution margins, fixed and variable costs, break-even points, and other profitability indicators.

  • Evaluate marketing investment efficiency through channel ROI, customer acquisition cost (CAC), lifetime value (LTV), cohort retention, and payback analysis.

  • Build financial business cases for new products, retail expansion, pricing changes, and capital investments.

  • Conduct scenario planning and sensitivity analyses to support strategic decisions.

  • Assess departmental and warehouse productivity, presenting findings and recommendations to executive and operational leaders.

  • Reporting and Performance Management

  • Lead monthly business reviews covering actual results versus budget and forecast, variance drivers, unit economics, operating margins, cash flow projections, and marketing performance.

  • Establish and maintain financial and operational KPIs, dashboards, and reporting frameworks tailored to departmental objectives.

  • Deliver performance analytics across Marketing, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Finance, including cohort analysis, SKU-level performance, overhead, direct labor, and ROI.

  • Prepare accurate monthly financial reporting packages for executive leadership, including detailed analysis and summarized insights.

  • Monitor manufacturing overhead costs per unit within bills of materials (BOMs) and direct labor costs across work centers.

  • Develop departmental, location-specific, channel-level, and SKU-level profit and loss statements.

  • Provide ad hoc financial reporting and analysis as needed.

  • Marketing, Operations, and Supply Chain Finance

  • Collaborate with department leaders on inventory planning, cost of goods sold (COGS), cost of sales (COS), landed costs, resource requirements, and working capital management.

  • Maintain and update financial forecasts within Acumatica.

  • Model the financial impact of changes in ingredient, co-manufacturer, freight, and packaging costs.

  • Monitor production-level costs and inventory impacts, identifying and reporting variances outside established tolerances.

  • Support departmental cash flow forecasting and capital expenditure planning.

  • Systems and Team Leadership

  • Develop FP&A tools, data flows, and automation within existing platforms, including Acumatica, Velixo, Mixpanel, and Logiwa.

  • Partner closely with Accounting to support timely financial closes and ensure accurate reporting data.

  • Establish FP&A as a distinct function from Accounting, developing its processes, reporting structures, and cross-functional partnerships.

  • Build, mentor, and develop the FP&A team, including recruiting and managing financial analysts as the department grows.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is a strategic finance leader with extensive FP&A and corporate planning experience, a strong background in financial modeling, and a track record of building effective finance processes and teams.   • 10+ years of experience in Financial Planning & Analysis or Corporate Finance.

  • 5+ years of experience in corporate planning.

  • Demonstrated experience leading or managing a Finance or Accounting department, including developing financial processes, reporting structures, and teams.

  • Professional experience in at least two of the following industries: e-commerce, retail, and manufacturing.

  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including complex financial modeling, data analysis, and reporting.

  • Proven hands-on experience developing sophisticated, driver-based financial models and converting financial and operational data into actionable business recommendations.

  • Experience with enterprise-level ERP or financial management systems such as Acumatica, NetSuite, SAP, or comparable platforms.

The Director of Financial Planning & Analysis will establish and lead a dedicated FP&A function, overseeing financial planning, forecasting, modeling, and performance analytics across multiple business operations. Reporting to the CFO, this hands-on leadership role will serve as a strategic partner to executive leadership and teams across Marketing, Accounting, Supply Chain, and Operations. You will develop sophisticated financial models, establish performance metrics, and translate complex financial and operational data into actionable business recommendations. The role will also strengthen budgeting processes, improve reporting capabilities, and support decisions related to profitability, investment, and growth. This is an opportunity to build a finance function from the ground up within a growing, mission-driven consumer business.

The Director will take ownership of company-wide financial planning and performance management, building the processes, systems, and team capabilities needed to support sustainable growth and informed executive decision-making.

  • Financial Planning and Forecasting

  • Lead the annual operating plan and budgeting process across all departments.

  • Design and manage rolling monthly forecasts covering revenue, margins, operating expenses, EBITDA, cash flow, and cohort performance.

  • Develop and maintain the company's three-statement financial model and long-range financial plan.

  • Transition ownership of company-wide forecasting from an external consultant while improving budgeting and forecasting processes across departments.

  • Financial Analysis and Decision Support

  • Partner with department leaders to evaluate financial and operational performance, identify key business drivers, and recommend actions aligned with organizational objectives.

  • Analyze product and channel unit economics, including gross margins, contribution margins, fixed and variable costs, break-even points, and other profitability indicators.

  • Evaluate marketing investment efficiency through channel ROI, customer acquisition cost (CAC), lifetime value (LTV), cohort retention, and payback analysis.

  • Build financial business cases for new products, retail expansion, pricing changes, and capital investments.

  • Conduct scenario planning and sensitivity analyses to support strategic decisions.

  • Assess departmental and warehouse productivity, presenting findings and recommendations to executive and operational leaders.

  • Reporting and Performance Management

  • Lead monthly business reviews covering actual results versus budget and forecast, variance drivers, unit economics, operating margins, cash flow projections, and marketing performance.

  • Establish and maintain financial and operational KPIs, dashboards, and reporting frameworks tailored to departmental objectives.

  • Deliver performance analytics across Marketing, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Finance, including cohort analysis, SKU-level performance, overhead, direct labor, and ROI.

  • Prepare accurate monthly financial reporting packages for executive leadership, including detailed analysis and summarized insights.

  • Monitor manufacturing overhead costs per unit within bills of materials (BOMs) and direct labor costs across work centers.

  • Develop departmental, location-specific, channel-level, and SKU-level profit and loss statements.

  • Provide ad hoc financial reporting and analysis as needed.

  • Marketing, Operations, and Supply Chain Finance

  • Collaborate with department leaders on inventory planning, cost of goods sold (COGS), cost of sales (COS), landed costs, resource requirements, and working capital management.

  • Maintain and update financial forecasts within Acumatica.

  • Model the financial impact of changes in ingredient, co-manufacturer, freight, and packaging costs.

  • Monitor production-level costs and inventory impacts, identifying and reporting variances outside established tolerances.

  • Support departmental cash flow forecasting and capital expenditure planning.

  • Systems and Team Leadership

  • Develop FP&A tools, data flows, and automation within existing platforms, including Acumatica, Velixo, Mixpanel, and Logiwa.

  • Partner closely with Accounting to support timely financial closes and ensure accurate reporting data.

  • Establish FP&A as a distinct function from Accounting, developing its processes, reporting structures, and cross-functional partnerships.

  • Build, mentor, and develop the FP&A team, including recruiting and managing financial analysts as the department grows.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is a strategic finance leader with extensive FP&A and corporate planning experience, a strong background in financial modeling, and a track record of building effective finance processes and teams. They should be comfortable working across departments and translating financial insights into practical recommendations for business leaders.

  • 10+ years of experience in Financial Planning & Analysis or Corporate Finance.

  • 5+ years of experience in corporate planning.

  • Demonstrated experience leading or managing a Finance or Accounting department, including developing financial processes, reporting structures, and teams.

  • Professional experience in at least two of the following industries: e-commerce, retail, and manufacturing.

  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including complex financial modeling, data analysis, and reporting.

  • Proven hands-on experience developing sophisticated, driver-based financial models and converting financial and operational data into actionable business recommendations.

  • Experience with enterprise-level ERP or financial management systems such as Acumatica, NetSuite, SAP, or comparable platforms.

  • Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex financial information and strategic recommendations to both financial and non-financial stakeholders.

  • Strong strategic and long-range planning capabilities, including experience collaborating with different departments to define objectives and establish plans to achieve them.

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field, along with a Master's degree or Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) designation.

    • Preferred Qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience with Acumatica ERP, Velixo BI, and Mixpanel.

  • Experience using AI or automation tools to improve financial reporting, forecasting, and analytical processes.

  • Omnichannel business experience, including direct-to-consumer (DTC), Shopify, wholesale, Amazon, TikTok, and retail operations, with familiarity in trade spend and distributor economics.

  • Experience in inventory management, COGS, COS, and supply chain finance, particularly in businesses involving internal manufacturing and co-manufacturers.

    • Benefits:

  • Geographic-based annual salary ranges:

  • Tier 1 – Higher Cost Markets: $152,000–$185,000.

  • Tier 2 – National Markets: $138,000–$168,000.

  • Tier 3 – Lower Cost Markets: $125,000–$151,000.

  • Final compensation and geographic tier placement depend on primary work location, skills, experience, and qualifications.

  • Fully remote work within the United States, subject to approved-state restrictions.

  • Medical insurance with up to 90% of employee-only premiums covered by the employer.

  • 100% employer-paid employee-only dental and vision coverage, with dependent coverage available.

  • Generous paid time off and accrued paid sick time.

  • Six paid observed holidays and two paid floating holidays annually.

  • Paid parental leave after six months of service for eligible employees.

  • 100% employer-paid short-term disability, long-term disability, and life insurance.

  • Referral bonuses of up to $1,500 for successful employee referrals.

  • 401(k) or Roth retirement plans with up to a 4% employer match after one year of service.

  • Monthly product stipend of up to $300.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Payer Relations based in the United States. We are seeking an experienced healthcare payer relations leader to build and lead a strategic payer partnership function across the western region. This fully remote leadership role offers the opportunity to establish the processes, relationships, and operational foundations needed to support organizational growth. You will take ownership of health plan engagement and in-network contracting strategies, working closely with Growth, Revenue Cycle Management, Clinical, and Operations teams. As the primary representative to regional and national payers, you will strengthen partnerships, support patient acquisition, and expand access to integrated care for justice-involved individuals living with substance use disorders. This is a hands-on position in a fast-moving startup environment, combining strategic leadership with direct execution. You will have the opportunity to shape the function from the ground up and potentially build a team as the organization scales.

  • Develop and represent the organization's payer relations strategy across the western region, engaging national and regional health plans, including Medicaid, Medicare, and managed care organizations (MCOs).

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key payer stakeholders across contracting, network management, and executive leadership.

  • Establish the organization as a trusted healthcare partner, communicating its integrated, whole-person care model and value to the payer community.

  • Develop relationships with community partners to create effective referral pathways aligned with payer and value-based care objectives.

  • Own the end-to-end in-network strategy, from initial payer outreach and negotiations through contracting, enrollment, and go-live readiness.

  • Lead payer negotiations and contracting discussions to secure reimbursement arrangements that support the care model and long-term scalability.

  • Oversee provider enrollment and credentialing workflows, ensuring compliance with state-specific and payer-specific requirements while minimizing delays.

  • Collaborate with Practice Management and Clinical teams to develop and present data-driven evidence of clinical outcomes and economic value to payers.

  • Partner closely with Growth and Revenue Cycle Management teams to identify and resolve payer-related barriers affecting patient access, operations, and revenue.

  • Build the payer relations function from the ground up, including workflows, tracking systems, templates, tools, and repeatable best practices.

  • Establish clear timelines, accountability measures, and follow-up processes to keep payer initiatives progressing and ensure timely execution.

  • Create scalable processes that support continuity and operational consistency, with the opportunity to recruit and manage a junior team member as the function develops.

    • Requirements:

  • Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Public Health, Finance, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

  • At least 7 years of experience in healthcare payer relations, provider network operations, contracting, or health plan partnerships.

  • Demonstrated success establishing payer relationships and translating them into measurable outcomes.

  • Hands-on experience developing in-network strategies and managing payer contracting processes.

  • Strong working knowledge of Medicare, Medicaid, and managed care organizations (MCOs), including enrollment procedures and payer-specific requirements.

  • Experience overseeing provider enrollment and credentialing workflows across relevant markets.

  • Proven ability to collaborate with Revenue Cycle Management, Operations, and Clinical teams to resolve payer-related challenges.

  • Strong organizational and process-management skills, with the ability to oversee multiple payer workstreams and competing priorities simultaneously.

  • Ability to operate effectively in an early-stage startup environment characterized by ambiguity, urgency, and evolving priorities.

  • Comfortable combining strategic leadership with hands-on execution rather than delegating all operational responsibilities.

  • Excellent relationship-building, communication, negotiation, and follow-through skills.

  • A collaborative, humble, curious, and team-oriented approach.

    • Preferred qualifications:

  • Advanced degree such as an MBA, MHA, or MPH.

  • Experience supporting multi-state expansion or new-market launches.

  • Background in behavioral health, substance use disorder (SUD) treatment, complex care, or other high-touch clinical models.

  • Familiarity with payer authorization requirements and operational workflows that affect patient access and billing.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Legal, Risk & Compliance based in United States. The Director, Legal, Risk & Compliance will lead and develop an integrated enterprise function overseeing legal affairs, risk management, regulatory and donor compliance, ethics, integrity, and safeguarding. This strategic leadership position will play a critical role in protecting organizational interests, strengthening institutional accountability, and supporting responsible operations across a complex international environment. Working closely with executive leadership, country offices, and cross-functional teams, you will establish effective frameworks, policies, and systems to identify and manage material risks. The role combines enterprise-level strategy with hands-on operational problem-solving and offers the opportunity to shape organizational governance and decision-making. This is an impactful opportunity to build a mature, sustainable risk and compliance function within a globally connected organization.

  • Build, lead, and continuously strengthen the integrated Legal, Risk & Compliance function, establishing its operating model, strategic priorities, service approach, policies, standards, and systems.

  • Lead the enterprise risk management framework, including risk assessment methodologies, escalation criteria, reporting standards, and risk-informed decision-making processes. Advise enterprise risk owners and maintain visibility into significant institutional risks and mitigation measures.

  • Oversee the development and implementation of ethics and integrity frameworks, including codes of conduct, conflict-of-interest policies, anti-bribery and anti-corruption standards, whistleblower mechanisms, investigation procedures, and organizational accountability practices.

  • Lead safeguarding, child protection, and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) frameworks, ensuring appropriate policies, reporting channels, training, case management, investigations, and oversight mechanisms are in place.

  • Ensure that significant ethics, integrity, safeguarding, and compliance concerns are appropriately reported, assessed, documented, investigated, resolved, and escalated, including compliance with applicable donor incident notification and reporting requirements.

  • Provide and coordinate legal advice across institutional matters, including commercial contracts, intellectual property, corporate governance, employment matters, disputes, leases, trademarks, copyrights, and regulatory obligations.

  • Manage external legal counsel and specialized advisors across multiple jurisdictions, ensuring that advice is timely, cost-effective, appropriately scoped, and translated into actionable organizational recommendations.

  • Establish and maintain contract governance standards, including templates, legal review requirements, approval thresholds, escalation procedures, and oversight of significant or high-risk agreements.

  • Oversee the legal and regulatory frameworks supporting international operations, including country registrations, renewals, host government agreements, legal entity requirements, powers of attorney, banking documentation, and corporate records.

  • Lead the institutional compliance framework covering applicable legal and regulatory obligations, donor requirements, sanctions, anti-terrorism financing, data protection, incident reporting, and other relevant operational and programmatic requirements.

  • Direct the Grants, Contracts & Donor Compliance capability, providing institutional expertise, interpretation, due diligence frameworks, compliance standards, guidance, training, and appropriate review processes in collaboration with program, finance, and operational teams.

  • Lead institutional policy governance, establishing standards for policy development, ownership, approval, review cycles, exceptions, local adaptations, and centralized policy documentation.

  • Coordinate mandatory and role-specific training across legal, risk, ethics, safeguarding, donor, and regulatory compliance areas, evaluating its effectiveness in strengthening organizational awareness and accountability.

  • Maintain accurate institutional records and reporting systems covering enterprise risks, legal entities, significant legal matters, policies, safeguarding and integrity cases, compliance issues, corrective actions, and mandatory training.

  • Identify recurring issues, systemic weaknesses, and lessons learned from investigations, incidents, audits, compliance reviews, and country office experience, translating findings into improvements to policies, controls, and operational processes.

  • Provide executive leadership and governance bodies with clear, timely, and decision-oriented reporting on significant risks, legal matters, investigations, safeguarding concerns, compliance issues, and outstanding corrective actions.

  • Partner with country offices and enterprise functions to resolve complex legal, regulatory, donor, safeguarding, governance, and operational challenges through practical, proportionate, and risk-based solutions.

    • Requirements:

  • At least 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience across legal affairs, enterprise risk management, compliance, safeguarding, ethics and integrity, investigations, governance, donor compliance, or related institutional leadership functions, with meaningful experience across several areas.

  • Direct experience managing compliance and accountability requirements under U.S. Government awards, particularly those funded by the U.S. Department of State. Experience with Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)-funded programs is highly desirable.

  • Strong understanding of donor compliance and accountability requirements, including safeguarding and PSEAH, incident reporting, investigations, sanctions, anti-terrorism requirements, due diligence, sub-award management, contractual flow-downs, and organizational accountability.

  • Demonstrated experience managing legal matters and external counsel across multiple jurisdictions, ideally including countries in Asia and the Pacific. A formal legal qualification is not mandatory, but strong legal and regulatory literacy is essential.

  • Proven experience designing, establishing, or strengthening enterprise risk management and accountability systems, including compliance frameworks, safeguarding programs, ethics and investigations processes, legal governance, policy management, or case management systems.

  • Ability to translate complex legal, regulatory, donor, risk, and safeguarding requirements into practical institutional policies, procedures, controls, training programs, reporting mechanisms, and operational solutions.

  • Strong analytical capabilities and sound professional judgment, with experience assessing sensitive or complex matters, identifying material organizational exposure, evaluating risks and trade-offs, and providing clear recommendations.

  • Experience working with senior executives, country offices, program teams, and operational stakeholders in international, decentralized, or multi-jurisdictional environments.

  • Excellent relationship-building, communication, and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across different functions, cultures, geographies, and levels of authority.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical matters into accessible guidance, practical recommendations, and executive- or Board-level reporting.

  • High levels of discretion, integrity, and sound judgment when handling confidential or sensitive legal, safeguarding, investigative, personnel, donor, and institutional matters.

  • Ability to balance strategic leadership with hands-on operational problem-solving, while building trust and promoting accountability throughout the organization.

  • A relevant advanced degree, professional qualification, or certification in law, risk management, compliance, governance, safeguarding, investigations, audit, or a related discipline is preferred.

  • 15+ years of relevant experience, including leadership of an integrated legal, risk, compliance, safeguarding, ethics, governance, or accountability function, is an advantage.

  • Direct professional experience in Asia and the Pacific, familiarity with the region's legal and regulatory environments, and experience developing enterprise risk or compliance reporting for executive leadership, Boards, or Board committees are preferred.

  • Experience leading organizational change and strengthening institutional risk management, governance, compliance, safeguarding, or accountability frameworks is highly desirable.

  • Must already be authorized to work in the United States and able to maintain the required work authorization throughout employment. Visa sponsorship is not available.

    • Benefits:

  • Annual salary: Expected compensation range of USD $141,000–$155,000, depending on experience, qualifications, location, internal equity, and organizational policies.

  • Work arrangement: Flexible hybrid or fully remote working opportunity, with the position based in the United States.

  • Location flexibility: Remote work or hybrid arrangements from the San Francisco office.

  • Time-zone flexibility: Preference for candidates located in or willing to work within the U.S. Pacific Time Zone, with flexibility to accommodate collaboration across international time zones.

  • International exposure: Collaboration with country offices, regional teams, and senior stakeholders across Asia and the Pacific.

  • Professional development: Exposure to complex international legal, regulatory, donor compliance, safeguarding, and risk management challenges.

  • Travel opportunities: Occasional domestic and international travel, including to Asia and the Pacific, as required by organizational priorities.

  • Inclusive workplace: Equal employment opportunities and reasonable accommodations for qualified applicants with disabilities.

  • Employment conditions: Full-time, regular, exempt position reporting to the Vice President and Chief Operating Officer.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Marketing Technology based in United States. The Director, Marketing Technology will lead the strategy, development, and evolution of the marketing technology ecosystem, enabling personalized, data-driven customer experiences at scale. This senior leadership role sits at the intersection of MarTech infrastructure, lifecycle marketing, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. You will oversee the platforms, data architecture, and technical capabilities that power customer engagement across email, SMS, push notifications, web, and in-app channels. Working closely with Product, Data, Engineering, Marketing, and Ads teams, you will shape the long-term technology roadmap and drive the transition toward AI-powered decisioning and intelligent campaign orchestration. You will also lead and develop a specialized team while making strategic build-versus-buy-versus-partner decisions. This is an opportunity to transform how a large, global consumer platform engages, personalizes, and builds lasting relationships with its members.

  • Lead the overall Marketing Technology strategy, defining the long-term vision, technical roadmap, and operating model to support personalized customer journeys and business growth.

  • Manage and develop the MarTech team, overseeing a Senior Manager, Marketing Technology, who leads the wider team, while defining future roles, capabilities, recruitment priorities, and professional development plans.

  • Build the team's expertise in AI-powered decisioning and orchestration, enabling the development and management of increasingly sophisticated customer journeys.

  • Evaluate the existing technology ecosystem, identify capability gaps, assess vendor solutions, and make strategic build-versus-buy-versus-partner recommendations aligned with business priorities.

  • Own the MarTech ecosystem across CRM, email service provider (ESP) platforms, customer data platforms (CDPs), decisioning technologies, and the AI/ML infrastructure connecting these capabilities.

  • Lead the strategy and infrastructure roadmap for real-time, one-to-one personalization across multiple customer touchpoints, ensuring relevant communications reach the right members at the right time.

  • Drive the adoption and full utilization of existing decisioning platforms across lifecycle marketing and customer journeys while partnering with Machine Learning teams to develop and implement an internal decisioning platform.

  • Establish a unified member identity strategy and oversee CDP evaluation, selection, and ownership to create a consistent, comprehensive view of customer interactions.

  • Collaborate with Data Science and Engineering teams to define data modeling requirements, member context architecture, first-party data strategies, and the infrastructure needed for advanced personalization.

  • Define the long-term decisioning architecture, determining how external marketing platforms should integrate with internal machine learning capabilities and centralized decision engines.

  • Oversee the operationalization of machine learning outputs, including propensity scores, churn predictions, and product recommendations, within marketing platforms and automated customer journeys.

  • Develop and formalize AI-assisted campaign workflows covering campaign creation, journey and canvas development, quality assurance, and execution automation.

  • Establish clear governance principles defining which campaign activities can be automated and which require human oversight, ensuring quality, consistency, and responsible AI adoption.

  • Partner with Product, Data, Marketing, Engineering, and Ads teams to align shared infrastructure priorities and ensure the MarTech roadmap supports broader organizational objectives.

  • Drive continuous improvement in marketing technology capabilities, platform integration, operational efficiency, and personalization performance.

  • 12+ years of experience building and managing customer journeys across lifecycle marketing, mobile applications, and web environments.

  • At least 5 years of senior leadership experience owning a Marketing Technology, Marketing Operations, or Lifecycle Marketing function, including responsibility for both a team and its technology stack.

  • Proven experience leading a MarTech function, evaluating technology vendors, identifying capability gaps, defining strategic roadmaps, and building or transforming marketing technology ecosystems.

  • Demonstrated experience designing and operating channel-agnostic, real-time personalization engines across multiple customer touchpoints at scale.

  • Deep hands-on expertise with modern CRM and email service provider platforms, including canvas architecture, triggered journeys, advanced segmentation, Liquid logic, and data feed management.

  • Strong track record evaluating, selecting, and implementing MarTech vendors, including business case development, RFP management, vendor negotiations, and technology transitions.

  • Experience developing and managing multi-channel lifecycle marketing programmes across email, push notifications, SMS, and in-app messaging, ideally within a large-scale consumer mobile application or subscription business.

  • Familiarity with web personalization technologies and the ability to deliver consistent, connected customer experiences across digital channels.

  • Experience implementing or managing a Customer Data Platform (CDP), such as Segment, mParticle, Tealium, Adobe, Hightouch, or Salesforce Data Cloud.

  • Strong understanding of unified customer identity, data modeling for personalization, first-party data strategies, and customer data infrastructure.

  • Ability to translate marketing objectives into technical requirements and collaborate effectively with Data Science, Machine Learning, Engineering, and Product teams.

  • Working knowledge of data warehouse and pipeline technologies such as Snowflake or Databricks, with SQL proficiency expected. Advanced software engineering expertise is not required.

  • Experience working with centralized machine learning platforms, shared feature stores, batch inference pipelines, and model scoring frameworks.

  • Demonstrated ability to operationalize machine learning outputs, including propensity models, churn predictions, and recommendations, within marketing platforms and automated customer journeys.
