Head of Master Data Lifecycle Management
San Francisco Office (Fremont St) | San Jose Office (First St) | San Jose Office (Zanker)

Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.



If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.





*Note: This position requires presence in our San Francisco or San Jose office location 4 days per week; Lambda’s designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.

 

Lambda is hiring a leader to own how product and infrastructure data is defined, governed, and changed across the company, bringing master data management (MDM) and product lifecycle management (PLM) under a single organization.

You will build and refine the function: setting the strategy, developing and implementing the platforms, hiring the team, and establishing the governance and best practices that keep the data trustworthy as Lambda scales.

You will own multiple areas that define how Lambda’s hardware, supplier, and infrastructure data is created, maintained, and trusted. These include: Master Data Lists (item, supplier, site), Product Structure, Change Management, Lifecycle and Compliance.

This will be a deeply cross-functional role. Hardware Engineering, Supply Chain, Data Center Operations, Finance, IT, and others, will be both contributors and customers of the relevant data, process, and tools. You will work closely with these stakeholders to earn their ownership of the data, understand what they need from it, and build a governed path that serves them rather than slows them down.

 

What You’ll Do

Strategy and vision

 - Set the multi-year vision and strategy for master data and product lifecycle management, and the roadmap to a trusted digital thread, aligned to Lambda’s growth and capacity plans.

 - Define the operating model and decision rights: which function is the system of record for each domain, and how data ownership is shared across Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, and Finance.

 - Make the build, buy, and partner decisions for platforms and integration, and own the business case and multi-year investment plan.

Governance and accountability

 - Establish and chair the cross-functional data council, and secure executive sponsorship and ownership of data across the company.

 - Set enterprise policy for product data, change control, and lifecycle, and hold the organization accountable to it.

 - Define the measures of data trust and process health, and report progress and risk to executive leadership.

Business outcomes and risk

 - Tie data and change processes to outcomes the business cares about: faster deployments, fewer wrong-revision builds, lower supply risk, and less stranded inventory.

 - Anticipate and manage enterprise risk in supply continuity, regulatory and export compliance, and hardware and firmware integrity.

 - Close the loop between field reliability and design and sourcing decisions, so lessons from the fleet shape future product choices.

Delivery and partnerships

 - Own delivery of the phased roadmap, including outcomes, budget, and the sequencing of work across data domains.

 - Build strategic relationships with software vendors, implementation partners, and key suppliers.

 - Represent the function with executive peers and the board-level stakeholders who depend on reliable infrastructure data.

People and culture

 - Recruit, develop, and retain a leadership team and a high-performing organization, building from a small founding team to a scaled function.

 - Foster a culture of shared data ownership and drive company-wide adoption, so the governed path is the easiest path for every team.

You

 - 10+ years in product data, PLM, MDM, or supply chain systems, with 5+ years leading teams that include managers.

 - Led at least one end-to-end PLM or MDM implementation, from platform selection through adoption, in a hardware or electronics environment.

 - Deep working knowledge of EBOM/MBOM structures, ECO workflows, approved manufacturer lists, and component lifecycle management.

 - Practical experience with data governance: ownership models, stewardship, data quality metrics, and cross-functional councils.

 - Experience integrating PLM and master data with ERP, procurement, and asset or inventory systems.

 - Strong vendor, budget, and implementation-partner management skills.

 - Ability to influence senior engineering, supply chain, and operations leaders without relying on formal authority.

Nice to Have

 - Experience in datacenter, hyperscale, AI infrastructure, server, or network hardware.

 - Familiarity with export controls and classification (ECCN) for accelerators and compute hardware.

 - Experience with DCIM or CMDB systems and with serial-level as-built tracking.

 - Hands-on exposure to commercial PLM and MDM platforms, such as Teamcenter, Windchill, Arena, Aras, Informatica, Reltio, or Stibo.

 - Experience standing up a function from scratch in a fast-growing company.

 - Bachelor’s degree in engineering, information systems, supply chain, or a related field; advanced degree a plus.

 - Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings such as P&IDs, equipment diagrams, and mechanical layouts.

 - Experience documenting maintenance activities using CMMS or maintenance tracking systems.

 - Experience working with rotating equipment, filtration systems, and industrial piping is a plus.

 - Ability to climb stairs, stand for extended periods of time, and safely lift up to 50 lbs.

ABOUT MATTER LABS

Matter Labs builds infrastructure for financial sovereignty. We pioneered zero-knowledge rollups on Ethereum and developed the Prividium platform to help financial institutions build and operate digital asset businesses with privacy and control.
The platform’s adoption spans global finance, from DTCC, a cornerstone of securities markets, to Cari’s network of 30 banks representing $10 trillion in combined assets.

We’re a remote, global team tackling hard problems in cryptography and finance. Expect autonomy, high standards and access to the best AI tools. Your work will help shape how financial institutions move and manage money.




THE ROLE

You join the Platform team, which designs and builds the ZKsync OS node. You own one or more of its core systems end to end: peer-to-peer networking, consensus, RPC, the sequencer or storage, depending on where your depth is. We are looking first for depth in consensus or peer-to-peer networking, and next in high-performance storage. You also bring new protocol features into the node, such as cross-chain interoperability and new zero-knowledge provers.

The Production Unit runs the node for customers, and the Platform team makes sure what it runs is correct. The role has no customer-facing work. When an incident touches a system you own, the Production Unit can pull you in during your working hours.

What you will do:

 - Own core node systems. Design, build and maintain one or more of networking, consensus, RPC, sequencing or storage, and decide how they evolve.

 - Integrate new protocol features. Bring features such as interoperability and new provers into the node without breaking existing behaviour or the upgrade path.

 - Design bugs out. Use the type system, architecture, property-based testing and fuzzing so whole classes of bugs never reach production.

 - Hold the review bar. Review your colleagues' code as carefully as you write your own, and expect the same from them.

 - Use AI with judgment. Use the best AI tools to move faster, and understand every line you merge, whoever or whatever wrote it.

Within a year, you own one or two of the node's core systems, and features land in them without regressions.




WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You have designed and built a core component of a distributed system, blockchain node or database: networking, consensus, storage, an RPC layer or similar.

 - You write strong systems code in Rust, C++, Go or a comparable language. Our node is written in Rust, and Rust is learnable here.

 - You use types and architecture to make invalid states unrepresentable, and you have used property-based testing or fuzzing on real code.

 - Your code reviews find real problems, and you can explain every line you ship.

 - You can take a protocol change from specification to a running system without breaking what already works.

Nice to have: Ethereum execution or consensus client internals; RocksDB or another high-performance storage engine; zero-knowledge provers; libp2p or a comparable networking stack; open-source systems work we can read.

If you meet most of this and the rest is learnable, apply anyway.





COMPENSATION AND WORK MODEL

 - Base salary range: USD 150,000 to 187,000 per year. Where an offer lands in the range depends on demonstrated scope and results against the bar described above. The same range applies wherever you are based.

 - Performance-based variable compensation and a long-term token incentive are additional.

 - Benefits (employees): medical, dental and vision from day one, global health cover for team members outside the US; 401(k) with a Safe Harbor match up to 4 percent for eligible US employees, flexible paid time off plus public holidays and two company closure weeks a year; six weeks paid parental bonding leave plus up to ten weeks paid birth recovery leave; confidential mental health support; a USD 2,000 home office stipend, a company laptop refreshed every three years, up to USD 400 a month toward coworking, and a USD 500 annual learning budget; company and team offsites.

 - Fully remote, from any country where we can hire. Your working hours overlap with European or US time zones. Time zones close to Europe fit the team best.

 - Full-time, as an employee or a contractor.

SUMMARY OF THE ROLE:

Maze is building the AI-native platform for application and cloud security.  - Build multi-year account plans that map business units, regions, executive sponsors and use cases across large, multi-company groups.

 - Find where n8n already runs inside your accounts and turn that bottom-up adoption into executive-sponsored, company-wide programmes.

 - Open greenfield accounts with research-led outbound to CIOs, CTOs, Heads of AI and platform engineering leaders.


SELL ON BUSINESS VALUE AT EXECUTIVE LEVEL

 - Connect n8n to the board agenda, from AI governance and auditability to efficiency and growth, and lead with outcomes rather than features.

 - Build business cases with real numbers that tie automation and AI agents to each customer's strategic priorities.

 - Multi-thread across engineering, IT, security, risk, finance, legal and procurement, and build champions who sell n8n when you are not in the room.


STRUCTURE, CLOSE AND EXPAND

 - Scope and negotiate multi-year, seven-figure agreements, including enterprise-wide licences, multi-region deployments and deals through system integrators and cloud marketplaces.

 - Run expansion cycles of six to twelve months and greenfield cycles that can stretch longer, through security, legal and global procurement.

 - Partner with Customer Success, Solutions Engineering and Partnerships on our biggest bets, and bring in n8n leadership at the moments that matter.


BUILD THE STRATEGIC MOTION

 - Help define how n8n sells to its largest customers, from deal structures to executive sponsor programmes and expansion playbooks.

 - Take what you learn in the field back to Product, Pricing and leadership.

 - Raise the bar for the AEs around you while staying closest to the customer.


REQUIREMENTS


MUST-HAVES

 - 🏛️ Strategic accounts: You have ten or more years of quota-carrying enterprise software sales experience, including at least three years owning a small named portfolio of strategic, Majors or Global 2000 accounts rather than a broad territory.

 - 💰 Seven-figure deals: You have closed and expanded deals worth €1M+ in total contract value, including multi-year and custom commercial structures, in cycles of six months or more.

 - 🧑‍💼 C-suite credibility: You build relationships with CIOs, CTOs, CFOs and the offices of the COO, and you can talk about their business as well as your product.

 - 📊 Value-based selling: You have built quantified business cases tied to a customer's strategic priorities, and you are ready to walk us through one in detail.

 - 🌱 Land and expand: You have turned one team's adoption into an enterprise-wide commitment and grown accounts across business units or regions.

 - 🎯 Still a hunter: Even with a named portfolio, you create your own pipeline through outbound and executive networking, and you are comfortable with greenfield cycles of 12 to 18 months.

 - 📈 Track record: You have consistently hit or exceeded quota over the past three years.

 - 🧭 Structured selling: You use a methodology such as MEDDPICC and navigate technical evaluations, security reviews, legal and global procurement.

 - 🛠️ Builder mindset: You want to help write the playbook rather than run an existing one, and you already use AI in your daily work.

 - 📍 Location: You are based in Spain, Portugal, Denmark, Finland, Belgium or the Netherlands, you already have the right to work there, and you are comfortable with regular travel to customers across the territory.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - 🛠️ Technical product background: You have sold developer tools, cloud infrastructure, data, AI, integration or automation platforms.

 - 🤝 Partner-led deals: You have closed deals with global system integrators or through AWS, Azure or Google Cloud marketplaces.

 - 🚀 Open source or PLG exposure: You understand how community adoption turns into enterprise revenue.

 - 🏦 Existing network: You already know senior buyers at large organisations in your territory.

 - Earn customer confidence. Serve as a senior security and privacy counterpart for strategic and regulated customers. Lead complex due diligence, executive conversations and escalations, and help teams navigate procurement, renewals and expansion without overstating our controls or commitments.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

An AI agent is only as useful as what it knows about your company. For many of the world's leading companies, that knowledge lives in Notion. The AI Knowledge & Capabilities team makes sure every agent working in Notion – built by Notion, by customers, or by other AI companies – finds the right answer, quickly and at a cost that makes sense.

We own the systems that make this work: search, knowledge, and memory. We also own the agent harness – the tools, context, and model choices that turn a model into a working agent. We decide what to build using evals, customer feedback, and product judgment. Our work reaches users directly, and other AI teams at Notion build on it.

We recently shipped Memories, so Notion AI, Custom Agents, and agents connected through MCP can learn and remember across platforms. We also shipped Auto, a model router that delivers frontier quality at 90% lower cost. Next, we're bringing memory, search, and the harness together into one system. Nobody has figured out how to package that yet – we want any company to get a great knowledge system for its agents with a click or a few questions.

You will be a technical leader for the team. You'll set direction across search, knowledge, and the harness, starting hands-on with making agents better and cheaper, and help define how Notion measures AI quality.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. 




WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE:

 - Set technical direction for search, knowledge, and the agent harness – make the architecture calls, run design reviews, and decide what the team builds next.

 - Make Notion's agents better, faster, and cheaper – starting with the harness: which tools an agent can call, what context it gets, and which model handles each request.

 - Lead how we measure agent quality – evolve the metrics and evals that reflect real usage, and use them to choose what ships.

 - Turn company data into answers agents can use – build agentic search and memory that give every agent the context it needs, at the right latency and cost.

 - Work closely with research – partner with Notion's model research team on evals, model choice, and models trained for agentic work, and get what works into production. You'll also work with search platform and AI product teams on work that spans teams.

 - Grow the team – mentor engineers, review designs, and develop the next tech leads.




SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: 

 - Production applied AI: You've shipped and iterated on production LLM or agent systems used by real users. You owned how their quality was measured, and you changed course based on what you found.

 - Quality, latency, and cost tradeoffs: You've traded quality against latency and cost in a production system, measured the result, and can explain what you gave up and why.

 - Technical leadership: You've owned the technical direction of a complex system, often across teams, and kept it sound as it grew. You don't wait for a roadmap – you find the problems worth solving, make the case for them, and go deep on the hardest ones yourself.

 - Product sense: You've shipped quality improvements users noticed, and you've shaped new products from scratch – from the data model to what users see. You can explain why they mattered.

 - Shipping something new: You've taken an idea from nothing to a product people use. You try new models and tools early, form your own views, and turn them into product decisions.

 - Making other engineers better: You mentor engineers at every level, guide their designs, and share what you know so it scales past you. Multiple engineers have grown by working with you.

 - Clear communication: You write clearly about tradeoffs, disagree directly, and change your mind when the evidence says to.




NICE TO HAVES:

 - You've improved LLM cost and quality directly – e.g. model routing, eval-driven harness or prompt tuning, or token efficiency in long-running agents.

 - You've founded a company or been an early engineer at a startup, and built systems that hold up at large scale.

 - Experience working closely with research or model training teams.

 💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.

THE ROLE

Orbital has been scaling fast, and we’re scaling or security and compliance with it. We're hiring a senior, NYC-based InfoSec Lead to own our information security due diligence, compliance, and vendor risk end-to-end bringing structure and consistency to work currently covered by outside contractors.

Now is the time to bring this function in-house, focusing on automating manual tasks (such as customer DDQs), enhancing our compliance stance, and ultimately securing the InfoSec function as a proactive enabler of our growth.

This is a full-time InfoSec role, working alongside our UK-based IT Manager. Whilst experience in IT operations or IT management is helpful, the InfoSec Lead and IT Manager report independently to our Head of Operations and own separate (but naturally interconnected) remits.

You’ll also work closely with Engineering, Product, Legal and our external Infosec support, to keep security and compliance embedded in how the business runs, not bolted on after the fact.

Based in the US, with ideally some flexibility to come to the New York office.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN




INFOSEC & COMPLIANCE DELIVERY

You will:

 - Own our InfoSec strategy and roadmap: set the direction for how security and compliance scale with the business, not just an executor; identify control gaps and weaknesses, prioritize remediation, and track it through to completion.

 - Own our risk program: run risk identification, assessment and treatment, keep the risk register current. You're making the call on what's an acceptable risk.

 - Own third party risk assurance, in both directions: run vendor security reviews for vendors we bring on (or are renewing with) and own customer & vendor due diligence (DDQs) when we’re the ones being assessed.
   
   - Pull in support required from the rest of the business and jump on client calls when needed to resolve DDQs.
   
   - Drive automation on the DDQ side specifically, so it doesn’t eat a disproportionate share of your time as the function matures.

 - Own our existing and future compliance certifications: you’ll be responsible for maintaining compliance with existing standards (ISO 27001 and SOC2 Type 2) and pursuing future certifications relevant to us. Management of the compliance program will be end-to-end, and involve ISMS management reviews, quarterly access control reviews, audit evidence gathering, scheduling and remediation tracking.
   
   - This also includes keeping policy & public-facing security documentation (eg. our trust centre) current - so certification is a continuously-run capability rather than a periodic scramble.

 - Partner cross-functionally: work with Engineering, Product, and Legal to embed security and compliance requirements into how we build and sell, and stay close enough to product changes that customer-facing security information is always accurate.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Significant senior in-house or scale-up InfoSec leadership experience: you've owned due diligence, vendor review, and compliance work end-to-end inside a fast-moving business, not just advised from the outside.

 - Strong understanding of cloud & cloud security, and ideally previous technical background in IT Security or SWE / DevOps.

 - A track record of scaling due-diligence processes, not just running them manually, you know how to spot what can be templated, automated, or self-served, and you make that happen rather than just wishing for it.

 - Comfortable being close to engineering: you don't need to write code, but you're happy sitting in technical conversations, understanding product changes, and knowing enough about IT systems to weigh in sensibly on security-sensitive changes.

 - Pragmatic and delivery-focused: you know the difference between a genuine risk and a distraction, and you keep due diligence and audit work moving at commercial pace rather than becoming a bottleneck.

 - AI-literacy with working familiarity with AI governance (ISO 42001, EU AI Act etc).

 - Comfortable operating independently: this is an individual-contributor role to start, with real ownership of the roadmap rather than a narrow, audit-only remit.

 - Working knowledge of privacy law is important (GDPR/CCPA/US state privacy laws) to partner with our legal function.




WHY THIS MIGHT NOT BE FOR YOU

 - You want to run day-to-day IT operations or manage IT staff. That sits with our IT Manager, not this role.

 - You prefer tasks defined and handed to you. This is a role for an independent decision maker... you're expected to identify what needs doing, set the plan, and drive it to closure yourself, not wait to be briefed.

 - You feel more comfortable with a narrowly-defined, audit-only remit. This role sits close to Engineering, Product, and Legal, and is expected to actively reduce manual DDQ overhead over time, not just process tickets.




WHY JOIN ORBITAL

 - Shape how security and compliance scale with the business... the processes and playbooks here are still being built.

 - Genuine cross-functional influence: you'll be close to Engineering, Product, and Legal, not sitting outside them.

 - Genuine momentum: $60m Series B, doubling headcount, expanding across two continents.

 - Work alongside a leadership team that treats security as a business enabler, not just a risk function.

🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on.

ABOUT US

Parallel is a web infrastructure company. Our products are used by leading businesses in sales, marketing, insurance, and coding to build best-in-class AI agents with flexible and powerful programmatic access to the web.



We've raised $230 million from Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia, Index Ventures, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, First Round, and Terrain to build the web for AIs. We're currently valued at $2 billion and we're forming a world-class team of engineers, designers, marketers, sellers, researchers, and operational experts to achieve our mission.




THE ROLE:

You will lead the team that owns the experience of every developer who builds on Parallel. Our Developer Experience team is responsible for how developers discover, sign up for, integrate, and grow with our APIs, from the first API call to production scale. This team owns every surface through which developers integrate Parallel, including our API, CLI, MCP, SDKs, and plugins. Your mission is to make building with Parallel easy, intuitive, and delightful, and to help us grow a thriving developer ecosystem.

You will hire, grow, and lead a team of product-minded engineers, set the roadmap for our self-serve platform, SDKs, and API ergonomics, and partner closely with product, design, and go-to-market teams. You will regularly write code and build applications using Parallel yourself, experiencing the product as a developer and using those firsthand insights to shape the roadmap. You will stay close to the team's technical work, join design reviews, dig into problems with your engineers, and talk directly with developers to understand where they get stuck.




ABOUT YOU:

You are an engineering leader who cares deeply about product experience. You have strong opinions about what makes an API delightful to use, grounded in your own experience building with developer tools. You know how to turn firsthand insights and developer feedback into a focused roadmap. You build teams with high ownership and a high bar, and you would rather unblock your engineers than slow them down with process.




YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE:

 - Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and professional experience

 - Experience managing engineering teams, including hiring, mentoring, and growing engineers

 - A background as a strong engineer building developer-facing products, such as APIs, SDKs, developer platforms, or self-serve onboarding

 - A track record of shipping product features end to end in close partnership with product and design

 - The ability and desire to stay hands-on, from writing code with the products your team builds to reviewing designs and debugging production issues

 - Hands-on experience using AI coding agents in your daily workflow

 - Experience with billing, usage-based pricing, or product-led growth is a plus

 - Experience leading teams at a fast-growing startup is a plus

ABOUT PLANE

Plane's mission is to build the infrastructure the world's work runs on. Every organization runs on three things: the projects it's driving, the knowledge it keeps, and the requests it fields. Plane brings all three into one open, adaptable platform: simple enough for any team to adopt, dependable enough for organizations to build on. And we are building it for a future where humans and AI agents do that work together.

 

Plane began in public on GitHub at the end of 2022. Since then it has grown into a work management platform used by teams around the world: 63,000+ stars, 6,500+ forks, and a contributor community that reads our code and files our issues. Organizations run Plane as a managed Cloud service, on their own infrastructure, or inside fully isolated environments. Building in the open keeps us close to users and raises the standard for everything we ship.

 

Plane is the #1 work infrastructure in aerospace, defense, financial services, and other regulated industries: organizations whose requirements for control, auditability, and data residency rule most software out. When the strictest buyers pick a system of record, that choice means something. Adoption is growing fastest on Plane Cloud and in sovereign clouds, deployments that keep everything inside a country's own borders and rules.

 

Plane is backed by top investors and built across San Francisco, London, and Hyderabad. We work in tightly knit teams, stay close to users, and care about the visible product as much as the unglamorous details that make software dependable. People own problems end to end, and we add process only when it helps the work.

 


HUMANS AND AGENTS

We believe the next decade of work will be done by humans and AI agents together. Not agents replacing people, and not a chat window bolted onto software built for humans clicking around, but both working in one system of action, where an agent's work is as visible and as accountable as a person's. 

 

Most software treats AI as a feature. We treat agents as a kind of worker, and that changes what the system underneath has to be. Agents are only as good as the context they can see and the state they are allowed to change, so shared context, explicit state, durable history, and accountable action are not items on our roadmap. They are the product. Plane is built so that when an agent acts, the humans responsible can see what happened, why, and on whose authority, and the record survives.

 

This is what the infrastructure is for: making the future where humans and agents work together useful, legible, and fully within the organization's control. Every role at Plane is some part of building that.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

Plane ships one product to three very different buyers: a team that signs up on Cloud in a minute, an organization that runs it on its own infrastructure, and one that runs it on machines with no internet connection. The same release has to be explained to all three, and the differences between what each one gets are real. You own the messaging system underneath that: what we claim for Projects, Wiki, Intake, and Plane AI, the proof behind each claim, and how a launch reaches the site, the docs, Sales, and the community as one story rather than three. You will work with product managers on what shipped, with Sales on the objections that decide enterprise deals, and with the community, who file an issue when a marketing page overstates the product.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own positioning for Projects, Wiki, Intake, and Plane AI, and the source of truth for every claim and the proof behind it. When someone asks whether we can say something, you decide.

 - Own how capability maps to edition and tier. Cloud, self-hosted commercial, and air-gapped customers get different things, and the page has to say which.

 - Lead launches end to end: narrative, plan, page, announcement, email, in-product copy, and enablement, closed out with a review that names what moved and changes the next launch.

 - Lead pre-launch quality gates for your domain

 - Partner with our automation engineers on scenario coverage as our approach to test architecture and ownership continues to take shape

 - Stay close to customer-reported defects, spotting patterns and feeding learnings back into planning rather than just fixing what's reported

 - Act as a "QA consultant" to your pod, helping engineering and product understand what quality coverage a project needs and who owns it




ABOUT YOU

Ruby Labs is opening a small, intensive school for people who want to become Growth Managers and have the mindset for it - not the CV.

We run high-volume A/B testing across multiple consumer products with millions of users a month. Our Growth Managers own the full loop: find the opportunity, write the hypothesis, build the variant with AI tools, run the test, read the result, document it. We've built a system for doing that well - standards, tooling, a Claude-native workflow - and we're now training people into it from zero.

This is not an internship where you watch. It's paid work from your first day, and you never pay for the school. It's a hands-on track that usually takes a few months, with exams along the way, and you do the work yourself.

How it works

 - Stage 1 - Growth School. Intensive self-study on how we run growth, plus the technical setup: git, Claude Code, deploying. Then you build A/B tests end to end on a practice product. Weekly homework and check-ins with the Head of Growth. The stage ends with an exam.

 - Stage 2 - Hands-on practice. You run experiments yourself, from the idea to the documented result. Experienced Growth Managers review and approve each step along the way.

 - Final exam - when you're ready, within a time limit set in your offer. A second exam and a live defence of one of your own experiments. Pass it and we place you on a product as a Junior Growth Manager as soon as a place is open, with a path to Mid based on results.

We'll be direct: not everyone finishes. We explain the bar in the interview, and you'll know where you stand along the way.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



 - No CRO experience required. Any career stage, and fresh graduates are welcome. We select on how you think, not on what you've done.

 - A quick learner. You pick things up fast, ask the right question, and notice what others miss.

 - An eye for what converts. You can look at a page and say what's wrong with it - and why a user would feel that way.

 - Analytical by instinct. Comfortable with percentages, averages, what a sample is; you'd rather see the number than guess.

 - Already using AI for real work. Claude, ChatGPT or similar - not as a toy. You will learn to build and deploy A/B tests yourself with Claude Code - no coding background needed. Reading up on Claude Code and git before you start will help, and we teach the rest.

 - Clear English, written and spoken. You'll write hypotheses, documentation and summaries every day.

 - Ownership. You don't wait to be told what to do next.
   
   


WHAT YOU SHOULD KNOW BEFORE APPLYING



 - The track is intensive: Monday to Friday, full days. It's a sprint of a few months, not a permanent pace. Around test launches we may ask for some flexibility with your hours.

 - There are exams and regular checks along the way. We go through the details in the interview.

 - Paid from day one. Pay while you are learning is lower than a full Growth Manager salary. Pay grows as you pass the exams, and once you are placed on a product it follows that product's Junior package.

 - You start as soon as you are hired. There are no fixed cohort dates.
   
   


WHAT YOU GET



 - A real system to learn, not a reading list: the same standards, tools and AI workflow our senior team runs every day.

 - Experienced Growth Managers who review your ideas and sign off each test before it goes live.

 - Hands-on work from the first weeks: you build experiments yourself, starting on a practice product, not watching others do it.

Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.



Job Overview

As a Mission Operations Engineer, you will be hands-on with the deployment, validation, and iterative improvement of our autonomous surface vessels. You will be a member of the Test & Evaluation element, the internal-facing element focused on structured testing for product improvement through software and hardware iteration. Your work will directly support both project-based deliverables (e.g., capability rollouts) and ongoing programs (e.g., V1 software release). You will help ensure our systems meet rigorous technical and operational standards through detailed testing, data analysis, and cross-functional coordination. You are able to meet deadlines and achieve desired outcomes as both an individual contributor and as a part of your team.



Responsibilities

How you support the mission

 - Develop deep understanding of vehicle HW and SW architecture, and how the vehicle operates as a integrated system.

 - Lead planning and execution of structured field tests for vessel performance pertaining to autonomous navigation, perception, communications, and sensor integration, among other vessel functionalities.

 - Diagnose and perform real-time troubleshooting of autonomy, networking, and onboard hardware or software during test events.

 - Implement solutions for testing, safety of vessel operations, and system robustness to maximize efficiency.

 - Own data logging and telemetry monitoring systems; ensure data integrity for post-test analysis.

 - Contribute to root cause analysis (RCCA) and issue triage workflows after field anomalies, with reporting to relevant review boards to eliminate repeat issues.

 - Maintain autonomous vessels and test environments, including vessel and support craft operations, through the use of telemetry tools and onboard diagnostics to enhance reliability of all equipment and products.

 - Ensure testing aligns with DoD performance, compliance, and safety standards when applicable.



How you support the team

 - Lead planning and execution of test cases to validate software updates, autonomy behaviors, and integrated system functionality.

 - Interface with autonomy, software, hardware, and systems teams to translate product requirements into field-validated test objectives.

 - Foster a collaborative and positive team environment, promoting open communication, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

 - Develop test procedures, checklists, and safety protocols to support repeatable and safe vessel operation and overall mission execution while eliminating process waste.

 - Create post-mission reports with detailed logs, data plots, issue summaries, and engineering feedback.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field

 - 1+ years of hands-on engineering experience (design teams and previous internships qualify)



Preferred Qualifications

 - Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills (HW/SW) and ability to work effectively in challenging field conditions such as off-shore in open water

 - Experience and knowledge of best practices in planning and execution of complex test operations involving autonomous systems

 - Knowledge of networking protocols and communication systems used in autonomous vessels

 - Systems engineering experience, ability to understand multi-disciplinary integrated systems

 - Experience with sensor integration such as EO/IR, radar, IMU, and data processing

 - Experience with integration and testing of multi-disciplinary integrated systems

 - Experience with robotics, AI, or machine learning applications

 - Familiarity with software development in Rust, Python, or other languages and CLI environment

 - Ability to clone repositories, create/check-out branches, cherry‑pick commits, and check status across multiple branches while testing features

 - Familiarity with maritime operations

 - Understanding of DoD requirements and standards for autonomous systems

 - Experience working with embedded systems and real-time computing

 - Job requires up to 50% travel.

Physical Demands

 - Ability to certify as “fit for work” by demonstrating ability to swim and tread water

 - Frequently and repetitively, lift, push and carry up to 75 lbs.

 - Will be exposed to marine environments, including sun, wind, rain, cold, and saltwater spray, often for extended periods

 - Must be able to operate in daylight, low-light, and night conditions using marine navigation systems and visual cues

 - Ability to perform physically demanding work for extended periods of time, up to 12 hours/day

 - The ability to carry 20 lbs. up and down stairs

Benefits

 - Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

 - Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

 - Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

 - Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

 - Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan

 - Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

 - Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

 - Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




JOB OVERVIEW

 

As a Mission Operations Engineer, you will be hands-on with the deployment, validation, and iterative improvement of our autonomous surface vessels. You will be a member of the Integrity & Performance element, the focused execution arm for high-priority validation efforts that strengthen product confidence, improve capability performance, and increase reliability. Your work will directly support both project-based deliverables (e.g., capability rollouts) and ongoing programs (e.g., V1 software release). This role spans the Joint Operations Center (JOC) - our centralized watch floor for monitoring, command and control, and real-time technical support of distributed vessel operations. You will split time between hands-on field execution and standing watch in the JOC, where you serve as the remote technical authority for teams operating around the world. You will also help build the JOC itself: the tooling, procedures, and escalation paths that make sustained autonomous operations repeatable. You are able to meet deadlines and achieve desired outcomes as both an individual contributor and as a part of your team.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES:


How you support the mission

 - Develop deep understanding of vehicle HW and SW architecture, and how the vehicle operates as an integrated system.

 - Lead planning and execution of structured field tests for vessel performance pertaining to autonomous navigation, perception, communications, and sensor integration, among other vessel functionalities.

 - Diagnose and perform real-time troubleshooting of autonomy, networking, and onboard hardware or software during test events.

 - Stand watch in the Joint Operations Center, maintaining situational awareness across concurrent vessel operations through live telemetry, video, and C2 feeds; detect, characterize, and escalate anomalies before they become mission-impacting.

 - Serve as the remote technical authority during live operations — triage autonomy, networking, and HW/SW faults from the JOC and direct afloat and shoreside teams to resolution under time pressure and degraded comms.

 - Support JOC watch rotations, including nights, weekends, and on-call coverage during test campaigns and customer operations; execute disciplined shift handovers and maintain accurate watch and event logs.

 - Implement solutions for testing, safety of vessel operations, and system robustness to maximize efficiency.

 - Own data logging and telemetry monitoring systems; ensure data integrity for post-test analysis.

 - Contribute to root cause corrective action (RCCA) and issue triage workflows after field anomalies, with reporting to relevant review boards to eliminate repeat issues.

 - Support day-to-day operation of autonomous vessels and support craft, using telemetry and onboard diagnostics to diagnose issues and improve reliability.

 - Ensure testing aligns with DoD performance, compliance, and safety standards when applicable.


How you support the team

 - Lead planning and execution of test cases to validate software updates, autonomy behaviors, and integrated system functionality.

 - Interface with autonomy, software, hardware, and systems teams to translate product requirements into field-validated test objectives.

 - Help stand up and mature the JOC: telemetry and C2 dashboards, alerting thresholds, comms architecture, standard operating procedures, escalation matrices, and after-action reporting formats.

 - Lead after-action reviews for JOC-observed events, converting watch-floor observations into RCCA inputs and durable product feedback.

 - Foster a collaborative and positive team environment, promoting open communication, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

 - Develop test procedures, checklists, and safety protocols to support repeatable and safe vessel operation and overall mission execution while eliminating process waste.

 - Create post-mission reports with detailed logs, data plots, issue summaries, and engineering feedback.

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field

 - 1+ years of hands-on engineering experience (design teams and previous internships qualify)

 - Willingness to support a watch rotation, including nights, weekends, and on-call periods during active operations

 - Up to 50% travel (moved it up from Preferred Qualifications)




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills (HW/SW) and ability to work effectively in challenging field conditions such as off-shore in open water

 - Experience and knowledge of best practices in planning and execution of complex test operations involving autonomous systems

 - Experience in an operations center, watch floor, mission control, TOC, or NOC environment - including shift handover discipline, event logging, and escalation under time pressure

 - Familiarity with C2 and telemetry visualization tooling (e.g., Grafana, Nominal, Foxglove, ROS-based tooling) and building operator-facing dashboards or alerting

 - Knowledge of networking protocols and communication systems used in autonomous vessels

 - Systems engineering experience, ability to understand multi-disciplinary integrated systems

 - Experience with sensor integration such as EO/IR, radar, IMU, and data processing

 - Experience with integration and testing of multi-disciplinary integrated systems

 - Experience with robotics, AI, or machine learning applications

The Mission Operations Specialist sits at the point where our vessels meet the customer. You plan and run ASV missions, provide on-site technical support to DoD partners during integration and operations, and coordinate the projects and programs that carry that work from concept to delivery.

This role requires frequent travel to partner and customer locations, domestically and internationally, up to 50% of the time.

You will work closely with team members, stakeholders, and other departments to ensure successful delivery of assigned project and program objectives.

Projects are defined as work that ends with the delivery of an expected outcome or end date. E.g. payload integration and demonstration of function.

Programs are defined as longer, less terminal workstreams such as ongoing product improvement and development roadmaps. E.g. supporting the ongoing development and testing of a vessel such as Corsair.

 

Responsibilities

 - On-Site Technical Support: Provide on-site technical support and assistance to partners and customers during product integration, installation, commissioning, and ongoing operations. Troubleshoot and resolve complex technical issues related to our autonomous surface vessels, systems, and software

 - System Integration: Collaborate with partners and customers to integrate our autonomous surface vessels into their existing systems and infrastructure. Ensure seamless interoperability and compatibility between our products and their operational environment. Support system-level testing and validation activities

 - Customer Training and Documentation: Conduct training sessions and workshops to educate partners and customers on the operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of our products. Develop training materials, user guides, and technical documentation to facilitate knowledge transfer and best practices

 - Remote Support and Troubleshooting: Provide remote technical support to partners and customers, leveraging communication tools and remote access capabilities. Diagnose and troubleshoot issues, guide users through problem resolution, and escalate complex issues to the appropriate teams for further investigation

 - Field Testing and Validation: Participate in field testing and validation activities at partner and customer locations. Collect data, assess performance, and provide feedback to the engineering and design teams. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to address any identified issues and implement necessary improvements

 - Customer Relationship Management: Build strong relationships with partners and customers by delivering exceptional technical support and fostering effective communication. Understand their needs, gather feedback, and advocate for their requirements internally. Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to define goals, objectives, and deliverables. Act as a technical liaison between partners/customers and Saronic internal teams

 - Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities for process improvements and product enhancements based on customer feedback and on-site experiences. Collaborate with internal teams to implement changes and contribute to the ongoing improvement of our products and services

 - Travel Management: Coordinate travel logistics and scheduling for on-site visits. Ensure timely and efficient travel arrangements, including transportation, accommodation, and necessary equipment

 - Planning: Work between internal and external stakeholders such as DoD customers, facilitating communication, managing expectations, and ensuring mission or program requirements are met. You will support the team through development of comprehensive mission plans, considering factors such as route optimization, environmental conditions, and risk mitigation to achieve desired outcomes.

 - ASV Operations and Monitoring: Operate ASV operations during missions, monitoring vessel performance, sensor data, and mission progress in real time. Troubleshoot technical issues and implement contingency plans to ensure mission continuity. Maintain situational awareness of maritime environments and adjust mission parameters as needed

 - Data Analysis and Reporting: Collect, analyze, and interpret data acquired during ASV missions to derive actionable insights. Generate comprehensive mission reports detailing key findings, observations, and recommendations. Provide feedback to the engineering and development teams for continuous improvement of ASV capabilities.

 - Compliance and Safety: Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, DoD policies, and industry standards related to ASV operations. Implement safety protocols and procedures to mitigate operational risks and ensure personnel safety.

Role Requirements

 - Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Advanced degree preferred

 - Minimum of 3 years of experience in a field support or customer-facing technical role, preferably with complex hardware or software systems

 - Demonstrated success in project coordination and leadership in current role.

 - Valid driver's license and willingness to operate company vehicles or rental cars as needed

 - Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with team members, stakeholders, and senior management.

 - Strong leadership qualities, including the ability to motivate and inspire team members.

 - Job requires up to 50% travel.

 - Able to certify as “fit for work” by demonstrating ability to swim and tread water, lift up to 75 lbs., and spend extended time periods on the water.

Qualifications

 - Prior SOF and Military experience working with the DoD or other government agencies is a plus or equivalent experience

 - Experience in maritime operations, particularly with autonomous or unmanned systems is a plus

 - Proficiency in mission planning software, GIS tools, and maritime navigation systems

 - Strong technical knowledge of autonomous systems, robotics, or marine vessels, including their integration, operation, and troubleshooting

 - Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, with a track record of diagnosing and resolving complex technical issues in real-world environments

 - Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

 - Customer-oriented mindset with a passion for delivering exceptional support and building long-term relationships with partners and customers

THE ROLE:

Savvy’s broker-dealer, Savvy Wealth Management LLC, is live and growing quickly as advisors move onto our platform. We’re hiring a Compliance Associate to own its day-to-day compliance operations and build an exam-ready program from the ground up. You’ll keep our regulatory calendar on track, run supervision and surveillance reviews, manage registrations, and make sure we’re always ready for a FINRA exam. You’ll report to our General Counsel & CCO, partner closely with Operations and Product, and use AI and automation to make compliance work faster and more reliable.



RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own day-to-day compliance operations for Savvy Wealth Management LLC, our FINRA member broker-dealer

 - Keep Savvy exam-ready: maintain control evidence, organize supervisory documentation and coordinate responses to FINRA exams, audits and regulatory requests

 - Run the broker-dealer compliance calendar so every filing, attestation and recurring review is completed on time

 - Manage registrations and licensing: Web CRD filings (Forms U4, U5 and BR), fingerprinting, Continuing Education tracking and state registrations

 - Run Rule 3120 supervisory controls testing, and support the Rule 3130 CEO certification and the annual compliance meeting

 - Conduct recurring surveillance reviews of electronic communications, outside business activities, outside accounts and personal trading, and advertising, and escalate issues to the CCO

 - Partner with the CCO to keep Written Supervisory Procedures and the AML program current as the business changes

 - Work with Operations, Product and Advisor Success so new advisors and products launch with the right compliance controls in place

 - Use Compliance Alpha, Global Relay and AI tools to automate tracking, attestations and review prep




MUST HAVE:

 - 4–6 years of compliance experience at a FINRA member broker-dealer, clearing firm, or RIA with a broker-dealer affiliate

 - Hands-on experience preparing for FINRA exams or regulatory audits, including gathering evidence and drafting responses

 - Working knowledge of FINRA and SEC rules for broker-dealers, including supervision (Rules 3110, 3120 and 3130), registration, communications (Rule 2210) and AML

 - Experience with Web CRD filings and registration management

 - Highly organized and detail-oriented, with sound judgment on what to escalate and when

 - Clear written communicator who documents decisions so they hold up to regulatory review

 - Comfortable using AI tools and automation to make compliance work faster and more reliable
   


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Series 7 and 24 licenses, or willingness to obtain them

 - Experience with compliance platforms such as Compliance Alpha, Global Relay or Hadrius

 - Experience at a fast-growing fintech or newly launched broker-dealer

 - Competitive salary and equity package

 - We offer a generous relocation package to help top talent make the move to our NYC office

 - Unlimited PTO + paid company holidays

 - Access to holistic medical, dental, and vision plans

 - Company 401(k) (including Mega backdoor Roth options), Commuter, and HSA/FSA plans 

 - NYC office in Union Square

 - Lunch and snacks provided in the office, & dinner if you stay late

 - Access to virtual mental health care (Spring Health) and health concierge (Rightway) to help you find the right care

THE ROLE:

Savvy is hiring a Senior Corporate Compliance Counsel to handle many of the day to day functions that help drive the goals and metrics of our Legal & Compliance Department. You will be responsible for negotiating and drafting contracts that bring independent financial advisors onto our platform. You’ll assist with annual compliance audit remediations, monitor compliance with SEC rules and regulations and create policies and procedures that serve as the foundation of our department. This is hands-on work with immediate impact. Savvy is an SEC-registered investment adviser and broker-dealer, backed by Thrive Capital and Index Ventures, that gives experienced advisors the technology and support to run their practices without the back-office burden. That model puts legal work at the center of the business: every advisor who joins signs an agreement our team drafted, every client relationship runs on our agreements and disclosures, and every new product or pricing model needs legal architecture before it can launch.

As a core member of an AI-forward legal team, you will work directly with our General Counsel and Legal & Compliance team, take on real ownership early, and help build the playbooks, templates, and AI tooling that allow our Legal & Compliance team to keep the organization running smoothly. If you want broad exposure to contract negotiation, securities regulation, and compliance, and you want to grow alongside a company that is still building its legal function, this role is built for you.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Draft, negotiate, and close advisor agreements, amendments, and client agreements, often on timelines tied to an advisor's move date, learning to balance speed with protection

 - Turn negotiation experience into playbooks with standard positions and fallbacks, and help build them into our team’s AI tools

 - Work closely with Sales, Advisor Experience, Operations, and Finance to understand the business behind each contract, so your drafting solves real problems

 - Resolve findings from compliance reviews and regulatory exams by translating them into concrete fixes to agreements, Form ADV and Form CRS disclosures, and policies, and document the work so it holds up with regulators

 - Monitor new SEC, FINRA, and state-specific securities rules and guidance, assess what they mean for Savvy, and brief the legal team with clear, practical recommendations

 - Research and write memos on federal broker-dealer and investment advisor regulations, as well as state law questions that shape how the business operates




MUST HAVE:

 - JD from an accredited law school and active bar admission in good standing (New York preferred)

 - 7+ years of legal experience at a law firm, in-house legal team, or regulator, with substantial hands-on compliance experience as well as contract drafting and negotiation experience

 - Clear, concise writing for business, engineering, and product teams, not just other lawyers

 - Sound judgment about what you can resolve on your own and when to escalate

 - An ownership mindset: organized, self-directed, and able to drive matters to completion without reminders

 - Enthusiasm for a fast-moving startup environment where priorities shift and processes are still being built

 - Experience with investment advisers, broker-dealers, fintech, or other regulated financial services companies

 - Familiarity with the Investment Advisers Act, Form ADV, Form CRS, Regulation Best Interest, or FINRA rules

 - Experience supporting regulatory exams, audits, or compliance remediation projects

 - Experience building or maintaining contract templates, clause libraries, or negotiation playbooks
   


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Comfort using AI tools in legal work, paired with healthy skepticism and the habit of verifying output

 - Experience with restrictive covenants, employment agreements, or advisor transitions

THE ROLE

Savvy is hiring our first dedicated developer experience engineer. Coding agents are already part of how our engineers work, but adoption has moved faster than our ability to make their output consistently good. Wrong code and weak architectural decisions still create review burden. We are hiring someone to treat that as an engineering problem, not solve it with a longer prompt.

You will own how developers across EPD interact with coding agents and with the systems around them. That includes the codebase itself, our internal skills and instructions, cloud coding workflows, agentic code review, CI, local development, testing, debugging, and delivery. You will have substantial autonomy to make cross-cutting decisions, change defaults, and set standards across the organization.

 

This is a hands-on platform engineering role. Most of your time will be spent building software and improving the environment in which developers and agents work. You will also talk directly with engineers, study where time and quality are being lost, test your ideas against real work, and help teams adopt better ways of operating. You will join our infrastructure and harness team and partner closely with infrastructure, security, data, and product engineers.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own developer and agent experience: Set the roadmap for how our engineers and coding agents navigate the codebase, use internal tools, run tests, review changes, and ship software.

 - Build the cloud coding experience: Build the developer-facing layer around our existing compute foundations, including task intake, environment setup, context, tools, permissions, observability, review, and delivery.

 - Improve agent output at the source: Change repository structure, interfaces, documentation, instructions, and feedback loops so agents produce correct code and sound architecture more consistently.

 - Engineer context deliberately: Design what agents receive up front, discover progressively, persist, compact, hand off, or discard. Choose models and reasoning effort based on evidence from the job, not habit.

 - Own our internal skills system: Raise the quality of our shared skills and instructions through clear contribution standards, evaluation, discoverability, progressive disclosure, maintenance, and pruning.

 - Fix everyday developer friction: Improve CI speed and reliability, local setup, testing, debugging, deploy workflows, and the other bottlenecks that cost engineers time.

 - Measure what works: Combine developer research and satisfaction data with DORA or SPACE measures and task-level agent evaluations. Inspect traces, establish baselines, and test whether changes improve correctness, reviewability, cost, latency, and human intervention.

 - Drive adoption: Work directly with engineers, teach effective practices, and turn successful experiments into defaults. When the root problem is the codebase or engineering process, make that case and help fix it.

 - Partner on safe autonomy: Work with our infrastructure and security engineers on sandboxing, credentials, approvals, auditability, and the controls needed to give cloud agents useful access without giving them unlimited access.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Exceptional with coding agents: You use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar tools for substantial work and can show how you decompose tasks, manage context, choose models, inspect failures, and consistently produce maintainable software. Faster output alone is not the bar.

 - Internal tools with real users: You have built developer tooling or a platform that engineers beyond your immediate team relied on. You learned from their behavior and support burden, not only from what they said they wanted.

 - CI or large-codebase experience: You have made a meaningful improvement to CI, testing, repository workflows, or developer productivity in a substantial, long-lived codebase.

 - Product judgment for internal systems: You can interview developers, separate symptoms from root causes, turn evidence into a roadmap, and say no to attractive work that will not improve the system.

 - Strong software engineering: You have built and operated substantial production software. We are open on language and framework, but you must be able to move from diagnosis to a durable implementation yourself.

 - Evaluation over intuition: You know that agent behavior is nondeterministic and changing quickly. You compare prompts, context, tools, models, and workflows against representative tasks rather than declaring success from a demo.

 - Cross-team influence: You can set standards and change defaults across teams without becoming a gatekeeper. You explain the evidence, earn trust, and remain accountable for the experience you create.

 - Pragmatic range: You are comfortable moving between platform code, repository conventions, evaluation data, developer interviews, documentation, and hands-on enablement. This is not a prompt-writing, DevRel, or framework-only role.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building cloud or remote development environments, coding-agent control planes, or secure execution sandboxes.

 - Experience building or operating an agentic code review system.

 - Experience designing agent tools, skills, context systems, memory, orchestration, or model-routing infrastructure.

 - Experience using DORA, SPACE, or similar frameworks without reducing developer productivity to a single metric.

 - Experience in financial services or another security- and compliance-sensitive environment.

 - You’re never tired of learning. You’re able to self-teach new platforms and ways of working.

 - You appreciate direct communication. You’re both an active communicator and an eager listener. You’re motivated by feedback and see every setback as an opportunity to grow.

 - You can pivot on the fly. We are fast-growing, so our priorities are constantly evolving. What you worked on last month may not be the same next month.

 - You have a humble and “can do” attitude. Our teams create high-quality work on quick timelines.

 - You want to be part of a winning team. We’re stronger together, and you’re a person who embraces being pushed out of your comfort zone.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

Enterprise Deployment

 - Enable Early Adoption: Deliver initial training and resources that empower advisors to quickly leverage Savvy’s software, tools, and financial products.

 - Deliver Speed to Revenue: Drive revenue results for the company by onboarding advisors quickly. Act as a day-to-day contact for advisors during the transition process.

 - Balance several onboarding and activation processes while maintaining clear communications with stakeholders and remaining adaptive in a rapidly evolving environment.

 - Monitor and report on transition progress and potential risk situations. Coordinate with the Client Servicing Team to ensure smooth client account transitions.

 - Raise the bar for the team: Build playbooks and templates the enterprise transition playbook and templates, track transition speed, and be the go-to resource for other Onboarding Managers on complex transitions.

 - Share lessons from enterprise transitions so the whole team gets faster.

 - Spot where our process breaks at scale and work with Product and Operations to fix it.
   


MUST HAVE:

 - Strong client relationship skills. You build trust, communicate clearly, and help people navigate unfamiliar processes and important decisions.

 - The ability to turn complex information into clear guidance, presentations, and training tailored to different audiences.

 - A collaborative, low-ego approach and strong ownership. You’re comfortable setting the plan, getting into the details, and following through.

 - Strong organization and prioritization skills. You can manage several workstreams, anticipate roadblocks, and keep people aligned on deadlines and next steps.

 - A drive to solve complex problems and turn what you learn into repeatable, scalable processes.

 - Comfort working in a fast-growing business where priorities evolve and you’ll help create the playbook.

 - The ability to learn new technologies, workflows, and industries quickly. Prior experience in technology, fintech, or wealth management is helpful, but not required.
   


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Prior work experience in the Wealth Management industry

 - Prior work experience at a high-growth start up

 - Prior experience in the financial services industry

 - Familiarity with advisor transition frameworks and the compliance and registration steps that come with them.

THE ROLE:

Savvy is scaling fast, and the transition team is how new advisors get from signed to fully live on our platform. As a Senior Client Transition Specialist, you will own the most complex advisor book transitions end-to-end (large books, advisor teams, Broker Protocol moves, multi-custodian repapers) and act as an extension of the Onboarding Manager across every onboarding in flight. You will set transition plans, assign and balance work across the specialists, coach them day to day and assist the Onboarding Manager with people management (formal direct reports expected in 2027), partner with the manager on complex issues and escalations, and build the processes and automation that let the team absorb more advisors without adding headcount at the same rate. You will run your own book and raise the bar for everyone else's.

Who you are:

 - You've done this before. You've owned advisor transitions end-to-end at a custodian, RIA, broker-dealer, or fintech, and you know what breaks a repaper or an ACAT before it breaks.

 - You're a step ahead. You see which transition is about to slip before anyone says so, and you act on it.

 - You're detail-obsessed, and you spread it. You catch the error others miss, and you teach the people around you to catch it too.

 - You make calls. Given incomplete data and a go-live date, you decide what blocks, what waits, and who needs to know, without waiting for permission.

 - You build leverage. You turn a one-off fix into a repeatable workflow, document it, and use AI as a default tool while knowing exactly when to verify it.

 - You communicate directly. You keep advisors, custodians, and teammates calm and informed under pressure, and you say the hard thing early.

 - You have a humble, “can do” attitude and extreme ownership. You want to be part of a winning team, and you embrace being pushed out of your comfort zone.

You will report to the Client Service Onboarding Manager.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own the end-to-end transition of Savvy's most complex advisor books across custodians (Schwab, Fidelity), from transition planning and paperwork generation through completed account transfers and handoff to steady state.

 - Act as an extension of the Onboarding Manager: own assignment of new onboardings to specialists based on complexity and capacity, maintain visibility across all in-flight onboardings, run the weekly portfolio review, and rebalance work as risks and volume shift.

 - Solve complex issues and escalations (NIGO, custodian, vendor, data, advisor) together with the Onboarding Manager: own the first response, resolve or route quickly, and keep the advisor informed throughout.

 - QA paperwork, transition spreadsheets, and trackers on high-risk books before submission; run root-cause reviews on NIGOs and turn findings into fixes.

 - Assist the Onboarding Manager with people management of the Transition Specialists: regular 1:1s, coaching on process, custodial platforms, and judgment calls, performance input, and onboarding new team members. Formal direct reports expected in 2027.

 - Lead pre-go-live transition planning with Sales and the advisor's team: data readiness, sequencing, standing instructions, and go-live risks.

 - Own and maintain the transition playbook; identify, build, and document process and automation improvements (including AI workflows) in partnership with Product and Operations.

 - Report on transition health (turnaround, NIGO rate, stalled accounts) and flag risk early to leadership.


MUST HAVE:

 - 5 to 8+ years in client operations, advisor transitions, onboarding, or account management in wealth management, with at least one full advisor book transition owned end-to-end.

 - Hands-on experience with Schwab and/or Fidelity custodial platforms and a deep grasp of account transfer, repaper, LPOA, and ACAT paperwork and NIGO resolution.

 - A track record of operating across many concurrent, deadline-driven workstreams and seeing risk before it surfaces.

 - Demonstrated judgment: you've made consequential calls with incomplete information and can explain how you decided.

 - Experience coaching, training, assigning work to, or QA'ing the work of others, with or without formal authority, and the desire to manage people formally.

 - Strong data hygiene and spreadsheet skills (lookups, validation, cleaning messy custodian exports) and the discipline to catch errors before they compound.

 - At least one process or automation improvement you built that other people adopted.

 - Fluent, daily use of AI tools for data and document work, with clear judgment about when to trust versus verify output.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, with the confidence to keep advisors and custodians calm and informed under pressure.

 - A collaborative, low-ego, self-starter attitude with extreme ownership, and comfort in a high-growth, constantly changing environment.


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience with Broker Protocol transitions, advisor teams, or books over $100M.

 - Familiarity with Orion, Salesforce, DocuSign, and bulk onboarding or CRM import tooling.

 - Experience building workflows or automations with AI tools (Claude, custom skills, scripts) beyond single-chat use.

 - Prior experience at a high-growth startup, custodian, RIA, or broker-dealer.

 - Experience formally managing a small operations team.

THE ROLE:

Savvy is looking for a Director of Advisor Onboarding to own and scale how wealth management practices move their businesses onto Savvy. When an advisor joins us, they're moving everything: their team, their clients, their systems, and the way they've run their practice for years. This leader makes that move fast, predictable, and something advisors feel great about.

Advisor Onboarding owns the advisor's journey from signature until they’ve established their practice at Savvy. The Director leads the team that runs this end to end: managing every workstream of the move, keeping the advisor confident and bought in, and enabling them and their team to work the Savvy way. For enterprise teams, the work looks a lot like a consulting deployment: learn how the business ran before, then map it onto Savvy.

This role reports to the Head of Advisor Success and partners closely with Growth, Product, Operations, Compliance,Client Experience, and IT. It's ideal for a senior operator who has run onboarding or deployment through hypergrowth, brings a consultative and commercial mindset, and has a strong executive presence with demanding customers.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own and lead the Advisor Onboarding function, including hiring, training, performance management, and org design for a rapidly scaling team.

 - Build and run distinct onboarding motions for enterprise teams and emerging advisors, with clear segmentation, staffing models, and playbooks for each.

 - Build an enterprise deployment playbook: discovery of how each team runs today, mapping their workflows and roles onto Savvy, and a tailored plan to get them live.

 - Own advisor enablement so advisors and their teams are confident in Savvy's tools and ways of working by the time they hand off to Client Experience.

 - Act as program lead across every workstream of a transition, coordinating Client Transition Specialists, Operations, Compliance, and IT to hit one plan and one date.

 - Own onboarding KPIs and OKRs, including time to start date, time to assets transitioned, onboarding CSAT, signed-not-started rate, and enablement completion.

 - Build a capacity model tied to the Growth forecast so the team is staffed ahead of volume.

 - Partner with Growth on late-stage enterprise deals: join recruiting meetings, scope deployment complexity before signing, and set expectations the team can deliver.

 - Design and own the handoffs from Growth into Onboarding and from Onboarding into Client Experience.

 - Own the team’s AI and automation stack: build the workflows, agents, and tools that cut manual work from onboarding.

 - Serve as the senior escalation point for high-stakes onboardings and fix the underlying process behind each one.
   


MUST HAVE:

 - 8 to 12+ years in onboarding, implementation, deployment, consulting, or business operations, with 4+ years leading teams in a high-growth environment.

 - Proven experience building and scaling an onboarding or deployment program through rapid growth (2x+ volume), including managing managers.

 - Experience moving customers' whole operations onto a new platform: learning how their business runs, redesigning their workflows, and driving adoption.

 - Experience running both enterprise (high-touch, complex) and mid-market (repeatable, volume) motions.

 - Strong program management across many parallel workstreams and teams you don't directly manage.

 - Sales acumen: has partnered with Sales on late-stage deals and is comfortable presenting to and managing senior, demanding customers.

 - Track record designing enablement and change management for experienced professionals.

 - Tech-forward operator with a track record of using automation and AI to improve speed and quality.

 - Excellent communication, executive presence, and cross-functional influence.


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Wealth management experience, especially advisor transitions (RIA, broker-dealer, wirehouse).

 - Experience at a recruiting-driven platform (wealth, real estate brokerage, healthcare practice platforms, PE-backed rollups).

 - Management consulting or implementation consulting background.

 - Experience leading or partnering on AI-enabled onboarding or service transformations.

As our Forward Deployed Engineering Manager, you'll build and run Savvy's deployment bench: a team of forward deployed engineers who go into the firms and advisor teams we partner with and make Savvy work inside their world.
