Senior Staff Engineer, System Architect - GCS & Fleet Management

ABOUT THE ROLE

Shield AI is seeking an experienced System Architect to shape the technical architecture of Hivemind Enterprise (HME) and help engineering teams translate that architecture into integrated, verified product capabilities. This is a senior individual contributor role for a technical leader who combines system-level judgment, software engineering depth, and the ability to bring teams together around practical technical solutions.

This role focuses on leading the technical definition for ground control system platforms, fleet management applications, and fielded tools that help teams rapidly refine autonomy using real-world operational findings. You’ll connect how autonomous systems are commanded, how software and configurations are managed across deployed fleets, and how operational experience feeds continued development.

You will work across the breadth of HME, connecting product intent, system requirements, software design, implementation, and verification. You will lead through technical credibility and influence rather than organizational authority, partnering with Engineering, Systems Engineering, Product, and Integration & Test (I&T) to resolve ambiguity, make sound tradeoffs, and maintain alignment through delivery.

This is a hands-on architecture role, not a design-only advisory position. You will actively participate in multi-team software development activities, help teams resolve implementation challenges, and use evidence from integration and test to ensure the architecture works in practice and remains sustainable as the product evolves.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Architect the platform for ground control systems: Lead the technical evolution of shared services, interfaces, data flows, and application foundations that enable ground control capabilities. Establish clear boundaries among platform services, applications, and vehicle-side autonomy, supporting consistent integration while allowing applications and autonomy capabilities to evolve independently.

 - Define fleet software management architecture: Architect capabilities for software distribution, deployment, configuration management, version and dependency compatibility, and fleet software-state visibility. Address controlled rollout, updated verification, recovery, and rollback across distributed assets, including environments with intermittent connectivity.

 - Connect operational findings to rapid autonomy refinement: Architect fielded tools and workflows that capture observations, logs, telemetry, configuration context, and operator feedback and enable authorized users to refine autonomy logic and behavior. Preserve the provenance needed to reproduce issues and assess deployed behavior, and define the path from field findings through modification, evaluation, validation, and controlled deployment, balancing iteration speed with safety, security, traceability, and recovery.

 - Define coherent, sustainable architecture: Translate product objectives and system requirements into implementable designs with clear component responsibilities, boundaries, interfaces, and data flows. Maintain a consistent system-level view, applying patterns that manage coupling and support reuse, testability, maintainability, and extensibility. Address architectural debt and balance near-term delivery with long-term product health.

 - Lead technical convergence and architectural decisions: Build trust, facilitate constructive disagreement, and bring engineering teams to actionable decisions through influence rather than reporting authority. Lead trade studies across capability, performance, reliability, safety, security, scalability, complexity, cost, and schedule. Clarify assumptions, constraints, ownership, and rationale; engage appropriate decision makers; and mentor others to foster shared ownership.

 - Carry architecture into implementation: Contribute code, prototypes, reference implementations, and reviews where they have the greatest architectural impact. Partner with teams to adopt and preserve design intent, close implementation gaps, and evolve the architecture based on implementation and test evidence.

 - Align requirements and verification: Partner with Systems Engineering, Product, Engineering, and I&T to define clear, feasible, appropriately allocated requirements. Align verification methods and acceptance criteria with intended outcomes, and use results to assess whether the implemented system meets those outcomes.

 - Maintain structured architectural definition: Maintain a version-controlled, traceable architectural model of system structure, behavior, interfaces, allocations, constraints, and decisions. Connect requirements, implementation, and verification evidence to support change-impact analysis and preserve decision context.

 - Track execution and surface risk: Partner with engineering leads to track architecture-critical milestones, dependencies, integration readiness, and technical issues. Surface risks early with clear impacts and mitigations, and help teams adjust scope, sequencing, or implementation to protect delivery objectives.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience: 10+ years of relevant experience in software development, software-intensive systems engineering, or system architecture, including substantial responsibility for the architecture and delivery of complex, software-intensive systems.

 - System-level architectural judgment: Demonstrated ability to decompose complex systems, define component interfaces and behaviors, evaluate architectural alternatives, and deliver solutions that span multiple engineering teams.

 - Software engineering depth and breadth: Strong hands-on development proficiency in one or more relevant languages, with working knowledge of technologies such as C++, Python, Go, TypeScript, and React. Ability to reason about design, integration, and technology tradeoffs across the stack, learn unfamiliar areas quickly, and engage credibly with specialists.

 - Cross-team technical leadership: A demonstrated record of leading through influence, resolving technical disagreements, and bringing teams with different priorities to a shared technical direction.

 - Implementation accountability: Experience staying engaged from architectural definition through software implementation, integration, and verification, including direct technical contributions that helped teams realize the intended architecture.

 - Decision-making and execution awareness: Experience leading trade studies, communicating decision rationale, tracking technical dependencies and progress, and escalating risks with actionable recommendations.

 - Structured technical communication: Ability to maintain clear, traceable architectural definitions and explain system behavior, design intent, tradeoffs, and risks to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

 - Distributed application architecture: Experience architecting software platforms or applications with distributed state, service interfaces, configuration and version management, or deployment workflows. Ability to reason about consistency, compatibility, connectivity constraints, and recovery across connected systems.

 - Education: Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.


DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Autonomous systems: Experience developing, integrating, or deploying autonomous systems, robotics, or software that interacts with complex physical environments.

 - Aerospace, defense, or safety-critical applications: Experience architecting and delivering systems where assurance, reliability, safety, security, and rigorous verification are central considerations.

 - Computing platform breadth: Experience architecting systems across a range of computing platforms and deployment environments, including cloud, on-premises, edge, and embedded platforms, with an understanding of their differing resource, connectivity, timing, and operational constraints.

 - Operational feedback and field iteration: Experience with telemetry and diagnostic pipelines, software configuration management, over-the-air deployment, or tools that connect field findings to reproducible evaluation and validated software or behavior changes.

 - Model-based engineering: Experience applying MBSE, SysML, and tools such as Cameo to represent system structure and behavior, allocate requirements, define interfaces, and maintain traceability across the development lifecycle.

ABOUT US

Our mission is to reinvent the way people learn, starting with language.

Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

We’re looking for our first security engineer: a hands-on builder who finds and fixes security problems. This isn’t a traditional security role focused on running scanners, filing tickets, and waiting for engineering to act. We’re looking for an engineer with deep security expertise who can build agentic workflows to remediate issues automatically and surface uncertain cases for review.

Speak handles voice recordings, conversation data, and payments for millions of learners, and our AI-powered product runs on streaming and LLM pipelines that bring their own new risks. The ideal candidate will have experience working in close coordination with product, infrastructure, and machine learning teams, and will be comfortable owning security end to end as our founding hire. There is no playbook yet, so you will write it. This role will be instrumental in earning and keeping the trust of our learners as we grow.




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Finding and fixing security issues across our backend, infrastructure, and apps: you write the code and ship the PRs rather than handing off tickets

 - Building secure-by-default patterns (auth, secrets, input validation, dependency hygiene) so every engineer gets the safe path for free

 - Securing how we collect, store, and process learner voice data and personal information across our AI and LLM pipelines, including prompt injection and data leakage

 - Hardening our cloud infrastructure and CI/CD: IAM, networking, secrets management, and container configuration

 - Setting up detection and response (logging, alerting, scanning) that surfaces real issues, then automating triage and remediation

 - Owning incident response end to end, from first alert to root-cause fix and postmortem

 - Laying the groundwork for compliance (for example SOC 2 and GDPR) and enterprise security reviews without slowing engineering down

 - Coaching engineers on threat modeling and secure code review so security scales beyond one person




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of industry experience as a software engineer or security engineer, preferably in a fast-paced startup environment
   
   - bonus: worked on a consumer app used by 1M+ users

 - A track record of fixing, not just reporting: you can point to vulnerabilities you found and remediated in production

 - Strong coding skills in languages like TypeScript, Node.js, or Python, and comfort reading and changing unfamiliar code

 - Hands-on cloud security experience on AWS or GCP (IAM, networking, secrets management, containers, infrastructure as code)

 - Solid application security fundamentals: authentication and authorization, API security, and OWASP-class vulnerabilities

 - Experience building detection and response, not just consuming dashboards

 - Excellent judgment about risk, and the communication skills to explain tradeoffs to founders and engineers alike

 - Ability to work independently as the only security person, and to coach and mentor other engineers
   
   Bonus:
   
   - Experience securing LLM-powered products or handling voice and audio data
   
   - Early-stage security experience, such as leading a first SOC 2 effort




WHY WORK AT SPEAK

 1. Join a fantastic, tight-knit team at the right time: we're growing very quickly, we've most recently raised our Series C from some of the top investors in the valley, and we've achieved product-market fit in our initial markets. You'd join at a magical time when a single person could significantly change the course of the company.

 2. Do your life's work with people you’ll love working with: we care strongly about our craft and want every person at Speak to feel like they're growing every day. We believe in the idea that working with people you both enjoy and have respect for makes everything better. We hire thoughtfully and only work with people we admire deeply.

 3. Global in nature: We're live in over 40 countries and launching in a number of new markets soon. We have dedicated offices in San Francisco, Ljubljana, Seoul, Tokyo, and Taipei, and you’ll have the opportunity to talk to users in each of these regions on a regular basis as well as travel.

 4. Impact people's lives in a major way: Learning a language is one of the single most life-changing skills one can learn, and right now 99% of people never achieve their goal because the process is broken. We’re helping millions of people achieve their goals and improve their lives.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots, shipping at scale to customers ranging from small manufacturers to some of the largest companies in the country. We're hiring a technical lead to build and run a central hardware testing function to support product development across the company. You'll set and maintain a high bar for product quality, plan and resource test work, build and run setups from quick bench rigs to long-running validation at scale, and help the team troubleshoot and root-cause failures. The work covers robotic and electromechanical systems of all kinds. Hands-on IC technical lead role, working closely with the mechanical, electrical, and software engineering teams.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Test Process and Quality Standards. Guide and build a test and validation team, working closely with the hardware team. Standardize how hardware product validation is planned and run, and work with the hardware team to set quality standards. Help turn requirements and specs into test plans.

Planning and Scheduling. Plan and schedule test work and assign lab space, equipment, and people to it. Work closely with hardware and software teams on priorities and timing.

Testbeds, Fixtures, and Ad-Hoc Testing. Help review, design and build complex testbeds and fixtures, including mechanical design, instrumentation, and data acquisition. Run one-off tests from a spec or setup the hardware team provides, and scale them up when needed.

Product Validation and Long-Running Tests. Stand up and run product validation testing across many units, from component qualification to system-level performance tests. Define stop conditions, data products, and post-run inspection, and keep long tests running.

Documentation and Analysis. Strong documentation is a core skill for this role. Write test reports and analysis, procedures, and initial failure analysis. Keep documentation accurate and up to date.

Troubleshooting and Root Cause. Help mechanical and electrical engineers analyze complex failures and perform maintenance to keep hardware running. Engage with engineering teams to respond to and resolve failures.


TOOLS

ABOUT US


Every 10 minutes, 18 million conversations happen between businesses and consumers around the world.


For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.


AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to interact with their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.


At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of agents to provide their customers with a new experience. But building a first agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.


We are a small, AI-pilled team that likes to solve hard problems. Be it engineering, product, or GTM - we build, experiment, and move fast, while heavily leveraging the capabilities of AI models. All of us like to challenge ourselves and take real ownership over what we do, all while still staying humble and keeping a low-ego culture.


Check out our principles https://principles.telli.com/ to see how we work.




YOUR MISSION

You will be the first BDR on telli’s Spain team, working side by side with our Country Manager for Spain. The product is real and customers across Europe use it every day; the Spanish sales playbook is still being written, and you will help write it.


We are outbound first. You will start conversations rather than wait for them: find the right mid-market and large companies, reach the people who own customer operations, and create qualified opportunities for the team. You will also help decide which messages, channels and routines become our Spanish sales playbook.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build focused account lists and find the people who have a real customer-interaction problem to solve.

 - Prospect every day through calls, email, LinkedIn and well-designed experiments. The phone is a core part of this role.

 - Run sharp first conversations: understand the workflow, volume, owner, urgency and reason to act, then hand opportunities to the AE with context they can use.

 - Test messages and sequences, measure what turns into useful conversations and qualified pipeline, and improve quickly.

 - Keep HubSpot clean and bring what prospects say back to the Spain team, product and marketing to sharpen targeting and messaging.




WHAT MAKES YOU A GREAT FIT:

 - You don’t need sales experience. Your background could be competitive sport, the military, hospitality, a call center or something else entirely. What matters is discipline, coachability, rigor and the ability to keep going through rejection.

 - You speak clearly, listen closely, are curious about how businesses run, and want to learn a technical product. You are comfortable picking up the phone.

 - You care about the quality of an opportunity, not the number of meetings on a calendar.

 - You take feedback directly, own your results and keep moving when the answer is no.

 - You bring a bias for action, aim for excellence, take ownership and work with low ego. Read the telli principles https://principles.telli.com/.

 - You speak and write excellent Spanish, work comfortably in English and are based in Spain.




YOU MAY NOT BE A GOOD FIT IF…

 - You don’t believe voice and conversational AI are the future of how people and businesses talk to each other.

 - You need inbound leads, a finished script or detailed direction before you can start.

 - You don’t like being on the phone. Calls are central to this role, so please don’t apply if you’d rather avoid them.

 - You resist coaching, or let a string of no’s stop you from trying a better approach.

 - You value meeting counts over understanding whether a prospect has a real problem and a reason to act.




THE REALITY OF THE ROLE

You will be one of the first people building telli’s business in Spain. There is no mature local demand engine and no perfect script to inherit. Outbound is the core of the job, and some ideas will fail. You will make a lot of calls, learn fast and help turn an early market into a repeatable business.
Success looks like three opportunities a week, across mid-market and large companies, that the AE accepts and can move forward. A full calendar without real opportunities is not success. If that sounds like the best challenge of your career, we want to meet you.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


1. CROSS-FUNCTIONAL IMPACT & RISK ANALYSIS

 - Build and maintain an enterprise change impact map: which teams, roles, processes, systems, and policies change because of the new business line, and how much.

 - Trace second-order effects across team boundaries, such as where one team's new process creates new work, handoffs, or failure points for another. Flag operational risks arising from the change, and solution mitigations with owners.

 - Working through functional leads, identify cross-team gaps and dependencies that teams have not surfaced themselves.

 - Translate impact into a clear "what changes for you" view per function, at both leader and frontline level.

 - Escalate cross-team conflicts and unowned gaps with a recommended resolution.


2. CHANGE MANAGEMENT, READINESS AND ADOPTION

 - Define the specific behaviors that must start, stop, or change per team, and the incentives, tools, or controls that reinforce them.

 - Partner with process owners to confirm new processes, roles, and handoffs are documented, owned, and understood.

 - Identify resistance hotspots and build targeted plans with the leaders who own them.

 - Design and run business readiness criteria and go/no-go checkpoints for each function ahead of launch milestones.

 - Develop the change, communications, and enablement plan, coordinating with functional leads.


3. STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT AND REPORTING

 - Define adoption metrics and track them through launch and hypercare (for example, process compliance, error rates, ticket volume, time to proficiency).

 - Coach executive sponsors and functional leaders on their role in visibly leading the change.

 - Provide a regular readiness and impact readout to Senior Leadership Team.

 - Hand off playbooks, impact maps, and sustainment plans so internal teams own the change after the contract ends.


SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

No function surprised at launch; every material process change has a named owner; readiness criteria met by launch date; adoption metrics on target within 60 days of launch.




QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED

 - 7+ years in organizational change management, business readiness, or transformation consulting.

 - Led change for three or more new business line launches, market entries, or operating-model changes, each touching 5+ functions, at least one end to end as the change lead.

 - Proven change impact assessment and stakeholder analysis across Sales, Operations, Care, Finance,  Product, and cross-functional teams.

 - Expert in application of structured change methodologies (Prosci ADKAR, Kotter, or equivalent), able to adapt them to the business.

 - Strong written synthesis: turns messy cross-team inputs into one-page impact and readiness views.


PREFERRED

 - Prosci Certified Change Practitioner or ACMP CCMP.

 - Background in consumer hardware, connected fitness, subscription, or DTC/retail.

 - Experience with operational risk frameworks or launch risk registers.

 - Comfort with Jira, Confluence, Coda, or similar program tooling.

BUILD A SAFER WORLD.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.


ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a single-customer Deployment Strategist role dedicated to a large government contract. Reporting into Customer Success, you'll be the embedded partner accountable for the customer’s success on TRM's AI investigation platform — owning adoption, value realization, and the trajectory of the account over a multi-year horizon, and coordinating the embedded TRM team to make sure outcomes are achieved.

Early on, the work is equal parts standing up value and architecting the program: onboarding users, running trainings, and capturing wins so the customer feels TRM's impact from day one — while also defining the operating model, cadences, metrics, and the roadmap for how the account matures. As it does, more day-to-day execution shifts to the customer's own team and you move into the full steady-state DS remit — sustained adoption, reporting, business reviews, and the partnership that underpins renewal and expansion.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Account success & value realization — you own the outcome: adoption, mission impact, and the value story that carries renewal and expansion.

 - Program architecture & governance — define the operating model, cadences, decision rights, and escalation paths; own the program charter and keep it current.

 - Embedded team coordination — coordinate across the embedded TRM team, keeping it aligned and driving toward the outcomes the customer is counting on.

 - Metric design & tracking — determine what gets measured (mission outcomes, platform usage, capability maturity), wire up the dashboards, and own the story the numbers tell — reported both internally and to the customer.

 - Workload & transition strategy — author and drive the roadmap for shifting workflows from TRM-led to customer-led, deciding which move, on what timeline, and under what conditions, evolving the model from TRM-heavy to partnership to advisory.

 - Adoption & enablement — onboard new platform users, field customer questions, and make sure users reach their first meaningful outcomes ("magic moments").

 - Training & readiness — host platform trainings for HQ and field, and partner with TRM Academy so readiness gates are met before users take on live work.

 - Value capture & communication — capture and record wins, communicate that value back through the regular drumbeat (standups, MBRs, QBRs), and translate program outcomes into the option-year and expansion narrative (the data backbone, not the deal-owner).

 - Cross-functional coordination — act as the connective tissue across TRM — investigations, TRM Academy, Product/Engineering, and Capture/RevOps — keeping everyone aligned and unblocked.

 - Customer deliverables & sprint coordination — help the customer produce the administrative deliverables they need and support their sprint coordination.

 - Risk & issue management — maintain the risk log, flag threats to milestones, and drive mitigations.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Year 1: The operating model, governance, and reporting are stood up; users are onboarded and active; trainings are running for HQ and field; and you're consistently capturing wins and communicating that value back — TRM's impact is visible and documented, and a deliberate shift of routine work toward the customer's team has begun.

 - Year 2 and beyond: The account is in steady state on the full DS remit — sustained adoption, usage reporting, business reviews, deliverable support — with the customer owning more day-to-day execution and TRM's value clear enough to carry renewal and expansion.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Program management experience — you can own operating cadences, a multi-stakeholder roadmap, and cross-functional coordination without formal authority, not just track a schedule.

 - Comfort with ambiguity — there is no established playbook for this role. You find the gaps on your own and build the operating model, not just follow one.

 - Experience as a program manager with a government customer, or in a customer success, deployment, or strategist role where you ran real rollouts, ideally embedded with a single strategic account.

 - Experience running recurring reporting or business reviews with a customer (QBRs, MBRs, or similar) and owning the adoption and outcomes that support renewal and expansion.

 - Background in or alongside threat intelligence, scam disruption, cyber disruption, or critical infrastructure — you understand the mission and the stakeholders.

 - Experience delivering in or alongside government / public sector environments.

 - U.S. Secret clearance required.

 - Strong facilitation and communication skills — comfortable training both leadership and field users and translating usage and outcomes into a clear value story.

 - AI fluency — you use AI tools to work faster and sharper, and can reason about how an AI investigation platform changes analyst workflows and where human judgment stays essential, helping non-technical users build trust in AI-assisted outputs.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Familiarity with blockchain intelligence, crypto investigations, or financial-crime workflows.

 - Experience supporting federal law enforcement or national security customers.

LIFE AT TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

 - Priorities and targets to change quickly

 - Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

 - A high level of personal ownership and accountability

 - Close collaboration across teams and functions

 - Frequent, high-touch communication

 - Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

 - A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. 




LEADERSHIP PRINCIPLES

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

 - Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

 - Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

 - Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

At TRM Labs, our Deployment Strategy team is on the front lines of customer experience – bridging product expertise with exceptional customer support. The team ensures our customers receive timely, accurate, and high-quality assistance at every step. You will work daily with leading state and federal law enforcement agencies — providing value through expert guidance, responsive support, and trusted partnership.

As a Customer Success Manager on our Deployment Strategy team in EMEA, you will play a critical role in helping TRM customers realise the full value of our platform. You will partner with law enforcement and regulators to disrupt financial crime across the crypto ecosystem. You will manage a portfolio of strategic accounts, driving adoption of TRM’s tools, and ensuring customers achieve measurable, long-term impact.

The Impact You Will Have

 - Act as a trusted advisor, enabling law enforcement and regulators to maximise the effectiveness of our platform within their investigative, supervisory, risk, and compliance functions.

 - Confidently explain complex technical and investigative concepts, supporting customer teams in interpreting blockchain data, building cases, and conducting financial crime investigations.

 - Build and deliver product demonstrations tailored to investigators, analysts and supervisors across the public sector, showing how TRM can be used in real scenarios to uncover networks, follow the money, and disrupt financial crime.

 - Conduct structured training sessions to ensure TRM is embedded into customers’ day-to-day investigative and compliance programs.

 - Serve as the “Voice of the Customer” by channeling customer feedback to product and engineering teams to influence product direction.

 - Monitor customer engagement and usage trends, identifying risks and opportunities to drive measurable outcomes.

 - Proactively identify early signals of churn risk and implement effective mitigation strategies.

 - Establish a consistent engagement cadence with customer stakeholders to understand institutional priorities and emerging risks, proactively addressing challenges before they escalate.

What We’re Looking For

 - 5+ years of professional experience, ideally within experience in law enforcement agencies

 - High proficiency in English and French are required

 - Hands-on experience with virtual currencies and blockchain analytics, ideally within an investigative context; strong appetite to deepen expertise in these areas is essential.

 - Proven ability to structure complex problems, prioritize critical issues, and deliver actionable solutions.

 - Exceptional attention to detail and rigor, particularly in investigative contexts.

 - Ability to distill and communicate complex technical and investigative concepts to diverse stakeholders, from analysts to senior executives.

 - Comfort operating in fast-paced, dynamic environments where expectations and priorities evolve quickly.

 - Strong collaboration skills and ability to influence outcomes in cross-functional settings

 - Willingness and ability to travel occasionally for in-person meetings, trainings, or events.

About the Team

 - As a globally distributed team, we work across time zones to provide seamless support and collaboration for our customers.

 - The EMEA Deployment Strategy team plays a key role in this model, ensuring continuous customer engagement and partnership as part of TRM’s global coverage. Team members operate flexibly to collaborate effectively across regions and deliver impact where and when it’s needed most.

 - Our Customer Success Team is fully remote, thriving on asynchronous communication and collaboration through Slack channels and detailed documentation. We hold weekly Customer Syncs, bi-weekly health syncs, join our associated POD calls, and regularly engage with our customers.

 - As experts in our craft, we focus on providing support, driving value, and building meaningful relationships with our customers as trusted advisors. We are on the front lines of TRM, ensuring our customers get the most out of the product and bringing valuable insights back to the team.

Learn About TRM Speed in This Role

 - Real-Time Client Response: You’ll triage and resolve customer questions during time-sensitive events such as sanctions updates or critical investigations.

 - Expedited Trace Validation: You’ll coordinate with internal teams to validate traces and gather intelligence within hours, ensuring accuracy and speed.

 - Continuous Global Coverage: You’ll contribute to TRM’s 24-hour global support model, ensuring customers always have timely, high-quality assistance no matter their region.

At TRM Labs, we're building the technology that will safeguard this transformation.

As our Lead Product Manager for Financial Institutions, you will define and own TRM's product vision, strategy and execution for financial institutions globally. You will lead the development of next-generation financial crime prevention, risk intelligence and compliance products for banks, FinTechs and payment providers.

 - Modernize financial crime infrastructure: Replace fragmented, manual workflows with intelligent, scalable and integrated technology.

 - Build differentiated, enterprise-grade products that integrate seamlessly into financial infrastructure and customer workflows.

 - Shape commercialization, pricing, positioning and market expansion strategies in partnership with executive leadership and GTM.

 - Own measurable outcomes across customer adoption, commercial growth and product effectiveness.

 - Experience identifying untapped market opportunities and translating them into commercially successful products.

 - Strong commercial judgment and the ability to connect customer problems with scalable business opportunities.

 - Experience leading complex, cross-functional product initiatives from discovery through commercialization.

 - Exceptional strategic judgment, intellectual curiosity and the ability to make high-quality decisions in ambiguous environments.

 - An entrepreneurial mindset and a track record of owning business outcomes, not simply product delivery.

Experience in payments, fraud prevention, financial crime, risk intelligence, digital assets or compliance technology is valuable.

Why Join TRM?

 - Multiply your impact. Build technology that safeguards financial institutions and the millions of people who depend on them.

About Wayflyer

Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.

Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential, and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.

You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.

The challenge

Wayflyer's growth depends on knowing exactly who we can fund and how much risk that carries. This role exists to dig into the data behind every customer, business and financial, and turn it into decisions that let us fund eCommerce growth responsibly.

What you'll actually do

 - Discover the story behind the data - analyse financial and non-financial data on new and existing customers to understand how their business really works

 - Assess and quantify risk - learn to evaluate the challenges of running an eCommerce business and how Wayflyer can fund that growth responsibly

 - Connect with customers directly - join regular calls to deepen our understanding of their business models, funding needs, and future plans

 - Collaborate with management to build and implement new processes and products

 - Support sales and operations by understanding how they win and manage customer relationships

 - Learn our existing loan portfolio and portfolio management tools, including when to exit risky relationships

 - Collaborate across Wayflyer - partner with teams across the business to connect dots, share insights, and drive impact

What this role could turn into

This is a launchpad, not a lane. Past analysts in this seat have moved into Senior Credit Risk Analyst roles, crossed into Portfolio Management, and built careers in Commercial or Strategic Finance as Wayflyer's risk function has scaled.

Who thrives here

Someone insatiably curious about how businesses actually work, not just their numbers. You ask questions because you need the real answer, not because you're expected to. You think founder-first, you're comfortable presenting your own conclusions in a room, and you're ambitious enough to want to prove it fast.

We hire for range

You don't need years of experience, you need trajectory. A strong academic record in Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Law or Computer Science (completed or near completion) is your starting point. About Woven by Toyota Woven by Toyota is enabling Toyota’s once-in-a-century transformation into a mobility company. Inspired by a legacy of innovating for the benefit of others, our mission is to challenge the current state of mobility through human-centric innovation — expanding what “mobility” means and how it serves society.   Our work centers on four pillars: Automated driving technologies; Arene, our software development platform for software-defined vehicles; Woven City, a test course for mobility; and Cloud & AI, the digital infrastructure powering our collaborative foundation. Business-critical functions empower these teams to execute, and together, we’re working toward one bold goal: a world with zero accidents and enhanced well-being for all.   =========================================================================

Our team specializes in developing and advancing cutting-edge Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) environments to accelerate the evolution of autonomous driving technology. We utilize two key SIL environments, ClosedSILS and OpenSILS, leveraging their unique characteristics to efficiently evaluate and validate software. Additionally, we focus on addressing shared challenges, such as improving processing speeds, which are essential for enhancing development efficiency.

In ClosedSILS, the simulator is connected to the autonomous driving software in real time, forming a feedback loop that enables dynamic evaluation of vehicle dynamics and control logic. This environment is designed with precision in mind, as we strive to improve the accuracy of simulation models while ensuring that generated signals are correctly linked to actual vehicle behavior. Furthermore, we are implementing computational optimizations and load reduction techniques to accelerate the simulation process. These enhancements aim to boost both the speed and reliability of testing, thereby significantly improving the overall development workflow.

OpenSILS, on the other hand, leverages on-road driving log data to validate software behavior in an offline setting. A key focus here is achieving high fidelity in reproducing real-world phenomena, such as communication delays or processing delays caused by CPU load observed in physical environments. OpenSILS doesn't simply replay log data—it integrates adjustments based on the load and timing conditions recorded during real-world operation. This approach enables the environment to replicate situations under conditions that closely mirror those of the original vehicle. By doing so, we can analyze issues that occurred during physical testing, pinpoint underlying causes, and effectively drive improvements in software development.

A shared challenge across both ClosedSILS and OpenSILS is the need for faster processing. By optimizing real-time capabilities within the simulation environments, we aim to deliver highly efficient testing platforms that drastically accelerate software development cycles. These ongoing initiatives address critical issues of safety and reliability in autonomous driving technology while laying the foundation for future-focused development.

Our activities integrate simulation modeling, real-world data analysis, embedded system design, and comprehensive software development, creating an optimal environment for autonomous driving innovation. Working in this challenging yet rewarding setting will enable engineers to grow their skills while contributing to foundational advancements in next-generation mobility technology.

We are seeking driven individuals who are passionate about supporting the evolution of autonomous driving technology and actively contributing to the development and enhancement of SIL environments. We especially welcome candidates with the following skills and experience:

  • Data Analysis Skills: Expertise in leveraging real-world log data to accurately model and reproduce operational conditions such as load variance and processing delays
  • Real-Time Optimization: Understanding of computational optimization and parallel processing techniques to achieve high-speed processing within SIL environments
  • Commitment to Improving Accuracy: A deep understanding of simulation models and a drive to enhance the linkage precision between simulated signals and actual vehicle behavior
